g: 4WD · 90 km return · 8 hrs · Difficult (Black Diamond)
properties.d: The Upper Goulburn 4WD Touring Route starts at the historic township of Jamieson. It travels through State Forest and features mountain views and historic sites associated with the gold mining era. The route is approximately 90 km and will take a full day to complete if you wish to explore some of the points of interest along the way. Surrounded by bush clad mountains, the township of Jamieson is also worthy of a visit to witness the beautiful colours during the Autumn Festival celebrated during March each year
properties.a: Jamieson, approximately three hours drive from Melbourne, is the starting point for this 4WD tour. The tour commences from the bridge over the Jamieson River at the south end of Jamieson, heading south along the Mansfield - Woods Point Road.

properties.n: Aberfeldy Backroad Tour - Donnellys Creek Loop
g: 4WD · 80 km one way · 8 hrs · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with some 4WD experience or training. Head north out of Walhalla, passing Cricket Ground Track after 6km, which goes to the historic Walhalla Cricket Ground. At 10 km, veer right onto Binns Road. On your right pass the historic sites of Holmedale with views to your left of the Thomson Reservoir. At the end of Binns Road, turn left onto McEvoys Track which boasted many hotel sites in the late 1800s servicing travellers to the goldfields. Continue north towards Mt Useful. At 10.2 km from Binns Road/McEvoys Track intersection, turn left into Donnellys Creek Road. At 1.8 km along Donnellys Creek Road is the 1863 Edwards Reef Burial Ground at the top of a short track to your…
properties.a: Route Summary - Starting from Walhalla head north on the Walhalla Road. At the 10km mark veer right onto Binns Road. Continue on Binns Road for the entire length to the intersection of Springs Road. Turn left up Springs Road. After travelling 10.2km turn left onto Donnellys Creek Road. Follow Donnellys Creek Road for its entire length to the Walhalla Road. Turn left onto the Walhalla Road. Follow the Walhalla Road south until you get to the Dam Access Road (sealed road). From here you can turn right, and this will take you over the Thomson Dam wall and back into Erica. Alternatively, you can…

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Mt Baldhead Loop
g: 4WD · 188 km return · 8 hrs · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. This route is a full day tour but can be extended over two days if you wish to camp along the way. Head north out of Bairnsdale on Bullumwaal Road and turn left onto Lookout Road to Mount Taylor with opportunities for picnicking, mountain biking or walking. Return along Bullumwaal Road to Bullumwaal, continuing along the Bullumwaal/Mt Baldhead Road for 15.8km to Stuttering Fred Lookout. Continue along Mt Baldhead Road for a further 13km then turn right onto Marthavale Road to travel to Marthavale Hut on the Nicholson River. Continue down Nicholson River Track if you wish to do the optional side trip (Grade –…
properties.a: Head north out of Bairnsdale on the Bullumwaal Road and onwards toward Mt Taylor.

properties.n: Far East Gippsland Backroad Tour - The Mighty Snowy
g: 4WD · 294 km return · 4+ hrs · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. Although graded as “Easy – AWD & 4WD”, conditions will deteriorate considerably in wet weather This full day tour has camping, picnicking and walking track options scattered throughout. From Orbost, head out to the Princess Highway, turning right. Cross the Snowy River and turn left to go under the bridge onto Buchan-Orbost Road with views of the historic old rail trestle bridge on your left. Continue on Buchan-Orbost Road and follow signs toward Buchan. There is an optional side trip for 4WDs off the Buchan-Orbost Road down Sandy Point Track to Sandy Point (Grade – Difficult). Otherwise continue north along…
properties.a: Starting from Orbost’s main street Nicholson Street, head south towards Princes Highway to start the tour. Sections on the route are unsuitable for caravans due to roads being narrow and steep.

properties.n: Far East Gippsland Backroad Tour - Waratah Loop
g: 4WD · 196 km return · 4+ hrs · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with some 4WD experience or training. Although this tour has been graded as “Medium – 4WD”, conditions will deteriorate considerably in wet weather. Note that seasonal road closures apply to some tracks along this route so it cannot be completed during the wetter months of the year. One way travel also applies near Waratah Flat. The Waratah Loop will give you a taste of the Snowy River country, some rugged countryside and tall forests. Highlights when driven clockwise, in order of appearance are passing by the eastern banks of the Snowy River and then a detour down to Woods Point on the Snowy River. After your stop at Woods Point, return back to Garnets Track and head…
properties.a: From Orbost Forest Park, head north along Orbost’s main street Nicholson Street to start the tour. Note seasonal road closures apply from mid-June to end of October throughout the route.

properties.n: Far East Gippsland Backroad Tour - Stringers Knob Mottle Range
g: 4WD · 84.4 km return · 4+ hrs · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. This half day tour (84km) loops through the Mottle Range Flora Reserve taking in many stops along the East Gippsland Rail Trail and the historic site of the Stringers Knob fire tower. All which showcase fine examples of past engineering efforts of past generations. There are two “Optional Side Trips” which are available for the more equipped tourers, taking you down to campgrounds along the Snowy River. This main drive can be done in 2WDs in dry weather only or 4WDs year-round but note conditions will deteriorate considerably in wet weather. Highlights when driven anticlockwise, in order of appearance are the…
properties.a: Starting from Orbost’s main street Nicholson Street, head south towards Princes Hwy to start the tour.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Bairnsdale - Dargo
g: 4WD · 110 km one way · 1–4 hrs · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. The Bairnsdale to Dargo route explores the highlights of Mitchell River National Park, featuring great views and walks of varying difficulty to significant cultural sites and stunning lookouts. You can extend the time on this tour if you choose to take up any of the camping options along the way. The tour begins at Howitt Park in Bairnsdale. From there, turn right onto the Princes Highway, passing through town, and then take a right onto Bairnsdale-Dargo Road, following the signs to the Den of Nargun. Next, turn onto Waller Road to enter Mitchell River National Park, where you'll enjoy breathtaking views on…
properties.a: Starting from the centre of Bairnsdale, head west out of Bairnsdale on the Princes Hwy to start the tour.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Glen Willis Loop
g: 4WD · 79 km return · 1–4 hrs · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. The Glen Willis Loop offers an intriguing mix of natural and cultural heritage, with numerous spots to stop, camp, fish, or kayak along the Mitta Mitta River. Start from Omeo, following Creek Street into town, then turn left onto Great Alpine Road. Continue onto Omeo Highway and turn right onto Omeo Valley Road, heading to Hinnomunjie Bridge. This historic 1910 bridge crosses the Mitta Mitta River providing access to nearby campgrounds. Continue on Omeo Valley Road, taking a left onto Knockers Track to reach Knockers Lookout for stunning views of the cleared valley from 1,477 meters. Return to Omeo Highway and…
properties.a: The tour starts at Omeo’s Livingstone Creek Park, heading north on Day Avenue and onto the Omeo Highway. Roads subject to ice and snow during winter, chains should be carried. Knocker Track is gravel with road subject to flooding and snowdrifts.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Dinner Plain
g: 4WD · 99 km return · 4+ hrs · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with some 4WD experience or training. Dinner Plain Loop explores the back roads and walking tracks of Dinner Plain (subject to winter seasonal closures). There are walks and waterfalls to see with some spectacular views and you will cross Victoria River, a river which was subject to Victoria's first hydroelectric plant, built in 1908. The loop begins at Omeo’s Livingstone Creek Park, which offers mountain bike trails, picnic tables, and overnight camping facilities. From there, head onto Creek Street and then turn right onto Great Alpine Road toward Dinner Plain Village. This distinctive village, established in 1986, is Australia’s only freehold land above the snowline.…
properties.a: The tour starts at Omeo’s Livingstone Creek Park, heading southwest out of Omeo on the Great Alpine Road.

properties.n: Aberfeldy Backroad Tour - Jordan Valley - Victor Spur Alt Route
g: 4WD · 22 km one way · 4+ hrs · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with some 4WD experience or training. This side trip turns left off Walhalla Road onto Victor Spur Track, entering the Thomson Water Supply Catchment and towards the historic townships of Red Jacket and Jericho. Continue southwest to cross the bridge over the Jordan River. Turn left after the bridge onto Red Jacket Track, passing the old school site on the way to Blue Jacket. After Blue Jacket, continue onto Violet Town, also known as Jollys as it was founded by George and Mary Jolly in 1862, who grew fruit trees and vegetables. Retrace your steps to Red Jacket, its Red Jacket church, hotel, post office and sports ground and visit the historic Red Jacket Cemetery with…
properties.a: Turn left off Walhalla Road onto Victor Spur Track to commence this side trip.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Dargo to Swifts Creek - Wentworth Falls
g: 4WD · 28 km one way · 1–4 hrs · Difficult (Black Diamond)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with reasonable 4WD experience or 4WD training. This side trip off the main High Country Backroad Tour - Dargo to Swifts Creek detours to the headwaters of the Wentworth River and a challenging 3km return walk down to the spectacular Wentworth Falls. After the falls walk, return along McDonalds Road for 8.5km to King Street, turn left and travel 1.4km to Wentworth River and its understory of Omeo Gum (Eucalyptus neglecta). Continue along King St for a further 200 metres to the Jirnkee Water Race. This water race is renowned for its impressive length of 56 miles (90 kilometres) and was built during the gold mining boom in 1889/90 to bring water from the Wentworth River…
properties.a: From McDonald/Baldhead Rd, turn left onto McDonald Rd towards McDonald Hut. Continue for another 7.2 km to reach Wentworth Falls.

g: Walk · 6 km return · 1–4 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Many steps · Limited signage
properties.d: This walk follows a historic tramline where horses and later, steam locomotives once hauled logs out of the forest. Begin at the Powelltown picnic area across from the DELWP office. Follow the signs to cross the Little Yarra River and head up the stairs to access the old Reids Tramline route. Along the walk you will come across parts of the old tramway and relics of an old timber mill, before exiting the bush and walking west back into town. Within the township you will pass many historic buildings including The Uniting Church and the area's last operating timber mill.
properties.a: From Melbourne head out along the Maroondah Highway to Lilydale. Past Lilydale, head right onto Warburton Highway. At the township of Yarra Junction, turn right at the traffic lights onto the Yarra Junction-Noojee Road and travel 15km to Powelltown. The walk commences at the Powelltown Picnic ground across the road from the DELWP office.

properties.n: Beauty Spot Nature Trail Long Loop
g: Walk · 1.4 km return · 40 min · Grade 2.1
properties.t: Well formed track · Flat · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: This easy nature trail has long been one of Marysville’s most loved short walks. The trail follows winding Leary Creek, deep among the tree fern groves that are a feature of this walk. Beauty Spot is noted for its abundant bird life, which is at its noisy best at dusk and dawn. A number of interpretive signs along the trail highlight the flora and fauna that inhabit the forest.
properties.a: Beauty Spot Trail can be found on Kings road in Marysville. From the Information Centre in Marysville take Pack road to the end and turn right into Kings road. The Beauty Spot carpark can be found on your right.

g: Walk · 2.2 km return · 27 min · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: Tucked away in the Wilks Creek Valley below Mt Gordon, this gentle circuit walk is easily accessible from the centre of Marysville. The walk passes through a dry mixed species forest before crossing a wetland on boardwalks and steel bridges.
properties.a: The start of the walk is located near the junction of Aubrey Cuzens Drive and Barton Ave, 250m from the centre of Marysville. Follow Gilberts Gully Trail for 300m to a junction. The circuit can be followed in either direction from this point.

g: Walk · 11 km return · 3.5 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Very steep · Many steps · Sign posted
properties.d: The most challenging walk in the area, Keppel Lookout Trail climbs through Mountain Ash and Stringybark forest to visit four of Marysville's best lookouts. There are spectacular views across Marysville, Cathedral Range State Park and Steavenson Falls. The trail is fairly uneven and steep in places and walkers need to be self sufficient with food and water and wear sturdy footwear. The walk is best done in an anticlockwise direction, first crossing Robertson Gully before climbing steadily up to Keppel Lookout. The trail then traverses around the ridge passing Oxlee and De La Rue Lookouts before reaching the top of Steavenson Falls, before descending down to the base of Steavenson Falls.
properties.a: Start at the trailhead located on Falls Road (alternatively the walk can be started from Marysville by taking the Tree Fern Gully Walk towards Steavenson Falls, to join with the Keppel Lookout Trail). Once you complete the loop walk down to the base of Steavenson Falls, follow the Tree Fern Gully Walk back towards Marysville, before turning left on the loop track about 200m after you cross Yellow Dog Road, to return to the carpark.

g: Mountain bike · 4.3 km return · 1–4 hrs · Easy
Walk · 4.3 km return · 1.5 hrs · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: The attractive bushland linking the Steavenson and Taggerty Rivers allows walkers and cyclists to step back in time to Marysville's historic logging past. Sections of this mostly flat circuit follow old tramline alignments, which in places reveal the original timber sleepers on which the big logs were transported to the nearby sawmill. The Trestle Bridge was built to span a small gully and provide access to the timber on Red Hill. The Taggerty River Lookout offers views of the Taggerty River. Access to the trail is via the junction of the Lady Talbot Drive and Woods Point road junction. From the trailhead, follow the trail for a few hundred metres to the start of the loop. Head right and…
properties.a: From Marysville head north to the roundabout and turn right down Marysville Woods Point Road. The Michaeldene Trail starts at the junction of Lady Talbot Drive and Marysville Woods Point Road.

g: Walk · 0.7 km return · 30 min · Grade 2.1
properties.t: Well formed trk · Gentle hills · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: Wirrawilla Walk consists of timber boardwalk winding through cool temperate rainforest. The ancient Myrtle Beech trees and Southern Sassafras provide a dense canopy that shades the understorey all year round. Ferns, mosses and fungi love these dark, damp conditions and thrive in the moist soils below the boardwalk. Picnic facilities, shelter and a toilet can be found adjacent to the Wirrawilla carpark.
properties.a: From Healesville, head up the Myers Creek road for 13km. Take Sylvia Creek road to the right then continue on this well maintained forest road for 4.5km. On the hairpin bend you will find the start of the Wirrawilla carpark access road on your right.

g: Walk · 6 km return · 2 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Very steep · Many steps · Sign posted
properties.d: One of the most challenging but beautiful walks in the area, the Wilhelmina track begins at Water Gauge Camp and heads over the suspension bridge along the Murrindindi River Walk, before turning right at the junction. Here the track climbs gradually over rocky steps to the base of the Wilhelmina Falls. These spectacular falls flow all year and drop 75 metres down a steep granite rock face. After relaxing and taking some amazing photos at the base head up the metal stairs over and between the granite boulders to the lookout at the top of the falls. Here there are spectacular views of the surrounding mountain range and Mt Despair.
properties.a: From Melbourne - travel along the Melba Highway to the intersection of Murrindindi Road just before Devlins Bridge. Turn right and drive 10km to the Reserve. Drive south along Murrindindi Road for approximately 3 km until you reach the Water Gauge camping area.

g: Walk · 0.7 km return · 30 min · Grade 1
properties.t: Well formed track · Flat · Occasional steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: This short walk takes you to a viewing platform at the base of Steavenson Falls for great views of the waterfall dropping into a rockpool below. The gravelled path and falls are floodlit between dusk and midnight. For the more adventurous, just back from the bottom viewing platform, there are stone steps heading up the hill which take you up to another viewing platform at the top of Steavenson Falls. This is a steeper 1.6km return track with steps. Here you can look down on one of the highest waterfalls in Victoria and enjoy an impressive view of the tree covered Steavenson River Valley.
properties.a: From Marysville follow the signs to the Steavenson Falls along Falls Creek road. Park in the Steavenson Falls Carpark. Please note there is a small coin fee for parking at this site. From the carpark head to the base of the falls before taking the stone staircase to the right leading up to the top of the falls.

g: Walk · 33 km one way · 11 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: The walk follows old timber tramways (1908 to 1916) that serviced sawmills deep in the forest. Hundreds of kilometres of timber tramways once dissected this landscape. As you walk through these tall wet forests and sections of cool temperate rainforest, you will see sections of elevated timber tramway being reclaimed by nature. Past Dowey Spur Road, the track descends 415 metres in 1600 metres down the High Lead Incline (named after the high lead cable logging systems that carried logs through the air over this steep terrain). Past Highlead carpark the track crosses a couple of log bridges and then the main road at the site known as The Bump, the divide between the Latrobe and Yarra… This…
properties.a: From Melbourne, take the Maroondah Highway to Lilydale. Just beyond Lilydale, turn right onto the Warburton Highway and follow this to the township of Warburton, where you can visit the Water Wheel Tourist Information Centre (weekdays 10am-5pm and weekends 10am-3pm) for more information. You may choose to commence the walk from Warburton, however most walkers prefer to start from the Big Pats Creek Recreation Area, a further 6km from Warburton. To get there, continue through Warburton another 4km and turn right into Riverside Drive after crossing the Yarra River. After 600m turn left into Big…

g: Walk · 1.2 km return · 30 min · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Well formed track · Short steep hills · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: This walk takes you along the old water race previously used in the mining days, discover the old town water supply where water was delivered to the town using the old water race from the water race dam.
properties.a: Access from the mini golf course in the centre of Woodspoint.

g: Walk · 1.8 km return · 27 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: The trail begins at the far end of Carters Mill Picnic area, this walk takes you along the slow flowing and picturesque Plain Creek and returns along the old 1930’s relic Tramway Bridge. You also have the option of extending your walk and taking the Tramway Bridge Walking Track, this walk takes you to the remains of the old timber trestle bridge once part of the tramway used to transport fallen timber.
properties.a: From Mansfield follow the Mt. Buller Rd to Sawmill Settlement, turn left onto Carters Rd.

g: Walk · 0.8 km return · 30 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: A short pleasant walk along the Delatite River.
properties.a: Located at Forest Camp picnic area, off the Piries-Goughs Bay Road 15 minutes from Mansfield.

g: Walk · 5.52 km return · 2 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Limited signage
properties.d: One of the ultimate short walks in the Victorian High Country. At the beginning of the walk you are surrounded by tall Eucalypt forest then climb to Snow Gum woodland. The Summit Loop provides expansive and spectacular views over the Mansfield area, the Delatite Valley and beyond to the peaks of the Victorian Alps, this walk will have you in awe of your surroundings. The track also offers a link through to Doughtys Rd (Doughtys Road to Summit Loop return is 6.1km return)
properties.a: The walking track is best accessed from Timbertop Saddle picnic area and car park. From Mansfield follow the Mt. Buller Rd to Merrijig. Turn right onto the Howqua Tk, follow for 6.5kms

g: Walk · 1.5 km return · 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Gentle hills · Occasional steps · Limited signage
properties.d: This walk is a 1.5km circuit with the option of ducking down to the rocks themselves around 500m metres along the trail from the carpark end of the walk. Spectacular views of the rocks can be found midwalk on the main trail although caution should be taken around the cliffs near this section. The final section of the walk is back South along Kentucky Rd to the carpark. A grade 3 walking track taking you to the spectacular Nicholson Rocks.
properties.a: Nicholson Rocks is a short day walk located off Kentucky Rd approximately 15 minutes drive from the townships of Heyfield and Briagolong. The popular 4WD accessible camping area of Huggett’s Crossing is a short drive north from the Nicholson Rocks carpark.

g: Walk · 10.5 km one way · 4 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Limited signage
properties.d: This walk meanders along the scenic Avon River and provides rewarding views and access to the river in several sections including The Channels. Vegetation varies from riparian species and wildflowers to dry sclerophyll forest on the rocky outcrops above. This is the main walk in the Avon - Mt Hedrick Natural Features and Scenic Reserve and well worth a visit if you have the time. The campgrounds of Huggett’s Crossing and Dermody’s provide overnight camping options. A grade 3 walking track that meanders alongside the Avon river.
properties.a: The Avon walking track takes off at Huggett's Crossing picnic area prior to the campsites. Huggett’s Crossing is located around 15km or 25 minutes North of the township of Newry and can be accessed via Three Chain Rd and then Kentucky Rd. At the end of Kentucky Rd turn left onto Huggett’s Track and travel for 4km on this 4WD route to the Camping area. The end of the walking track is located at Wombat Crossing. To access Wombat Crossing from the township of Boisdale travel North on the Boisdale-Valencia Creek Road, turn left onto Luckman's Road then Right onto Back Wombat Road. The walking…

g: Walk · 3.5 km return · 2 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: An information board at the picnic area provides information about the walk. The walk mainly follows old water races that lead to Granite Creek. Along the way you will encounter old house sites, old dams, a battery site and diggings which include the Evening Star Mine.
properties.a: Granite Creek is accessible directly off the Bairnsdale-Dargo Road. From Stratford, head north on Briagolong Road, turning right onto Stockdale Road. From Stockdale, head east on Beverleys Road, before turning left onto Bairnsdale-Dargo Road.

g: Walk · 2 km one way · 45 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Limited signage
properties.d: A small gully provides just enough moisture to provide a much different range of plant species to that of the surrounding dry ridge. Fern Gully Loop is the shortest loop option in the Freestone network of tracks. Approximately 2km in length it provides a good idea of the different vegetation types around Blue Pool and the Freestone Creek. The track is named for a small section of vegetation which has established itself in a moist gully receiving slightly more moisture than the dry ridge above. Access to the loop begins West of the Blue pool swimming area. An old mine shaft is present along the track and although covered now it provides a reminder of the past use of this area and that…
properties.a: From Briagolong follow the Freestone Creek Road approximately 10km or 10 minutes to the Blue Pool carpark area. The loop is accessed from the West side of Blue Pool.

g: Walk · 4.4 km return · 2 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Limited signage
properties.d: This is a short day walk which explores the historic Black Snake Creek mining area Southwest of Dargo. The track meanders up the gully past old house sites and bridle trails to an abandoned battery and steam engine. The Kong Meng loop near the end of the track provides rewarding views of the Alpine National Park to the West including the Pinnacles and Billy Goat Bluff. It is named for the company which held the mining claim here for around three years from 1867. Walkers are advised to stick to the track as there are a number of old unmarked mineshafts in the area. A grade 4 walking track that explores the Black Snake Creek historic mining area.
properties.a: To get to the start of Black Snake Creek East Walk, continue northeast past Black Snake Creek Campground for approximately 1.9km, along the Black Snake Creek 4WD Track.

g: Walk · 0.5 km return · 15 min · Grade 1
properties.t: Well formed track · Flat · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: Gravelled paths wind around the arboretum, with views to the surrounding hills.

g: Walk · 1.2 km return · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted

g: Walk · 3.7 km return · 1.5 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: After leaving the Memorial, this walk takes you to the north above the Reform Mine entrance. Along this walk you will see the towns old water storage basin (1934) which has long since been replaced. This small reservoir held water that was gravity-fed into town. The climb follows the drier northerly aspect of Reform Hill to the lookout.
properties.a: The site can be accessed via the Reform Hill walking track network. The best starting point is Jones Reserve located on the Great Alpine Road in Myrtleford between the Hardware store and Rays Ski Shop.

g: Walk · 1.2 km return · 20 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Gentle hills · Occasional steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: The track makes a loop around a dam built in 1892 to provide a permanent supply of water to the town and railway station. It no longer provides water to Bright but makes for a pleasant short walk close to Bright.

g: Walk · 2 km return · 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: After leaving the Memorial, a steep track will take you past the entrance to the Reform Mine and an old ventilation shaft, which once serviced the Reform Mine. The track continues in a southerly direction where more sheltered conditions enable tree species such as Red Box and Long-leaf Box to flourish. The track then turns north onto a straight and moderate climb to the summit. Rest stops are provided along the way.
properties.a: The site can be accessed via the Reform Hill walking track network. The best starting point is Jones Reserve located on the Great Alpine Road in Myrtleford between the Hardware store and Rays Ski Shop.

g: Walk · 3.2 km return · 1.5 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: The steady climb to the top rewards you with views over Bright as well as Mt.Feathertop, Mt.Fainter, and Mt.Bogong, the highest peak in Victoria. Return the same way. Walk through native forest to the top of the hill for great views of Bright and the Victorian Alps.
properties.a: Walk or drive from Bright 1.6km up Mt Porepunkah Rd to Quins Gap (park off the side of the road) where the walking track starts on east side of the road.

g: Walk · 2.8 km return · under 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · Occassional steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: A gentle walk along the banks of the East Kiewa River. Stroll through riparian forest, with plenty of spots to watch the crystal-clear waters of the East Kiewa River. Along the track you will come across Mermaid Beach (250m) or Rockpool (800m), ideal spots for a picnic or a cool dip in the water. There is an option for a longer walk back to Mt Beauty via Survey Track
properties.a: The walk starts on the eastern edge of Mount Beauty, on the eastern end of Tawonga Crescent.

g: Walk · 3.2 km return · 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: A 3km loop walk through local forest showcasing the forest types present on the drier ridges.
properties.a: Access is via the Great Alpine Rd approx 2km from Bruthen township.

g: Walk · 1.6 km return · 30 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: This walk loops off Easy Magic Walk and follows the service track behind residential properties then turns left before Engineers Road through the forest to return to the Easy Magic Walk.
properties.a: Access is via the Great Alpine Rd approx 2km from Bruthen township.

g: Walk · 4.5 km one way · 2 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Gentle hills · Occassional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This walk commences at Deptford Picnic Area and traverses the slopes above the Nicholson River. The track passes through the forest over usually dry creek beds and provides views down to the Nicholson River. This walk traverses the slopes above the Nicholson River. The track passes through the forest over, usually dry, creek beds and provides views down to the Nicholson River. The track crosses Store Creek shortly before reaching Stanton’s Place picnic area. The same route is followed to return back to Deptford.
properties.a: Access to the walking track is from the western side of the Nicholson River at Deptford.

properties.n: Beauty Spot Nature Trail Short Loop
g: Walk · 0.4 km return · 9 min · Grade 2.1
properties.t: Well formed track · Flat · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: The trail begins in the shade, walking through towering manna gums. The 0.5km trail includes a fantastic boardwalk pathway through fern tree groves. There are a couple of benches along the trail and several interpretative signs if you'd like to know more about the flora and fauna native to this area.

g: Walk · 1.5 km one way · 45 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occassional steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: This loop starts and finishes at Poverty Reef, which can be accessed via the Lookout loop. This walk takes in the northern section of Reform Hill, formally the site of the school pine plantation and has been replanted with native vegetation since 2011. The walk leads to an excellent lookout, overlooking the Myrtleford township and the Ovens Valley.
properties.a: The site can be accessed via the Reform Hill walking track network. From Jones Reserve, follow the Lookout Loop track north. You will pass the Hume and Hovell monument and the old water storage basin. Poverty Reef Loop starts and finishes from the same location on the Lookout Loop

g: Walk · 2.4 km return · under 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occassional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Store Point was once a township established for the Donnellys Creek gold mining boom in the 1860s. The Store Point Historic Loop Walk starts from the Store Point Hut, and follows McKean Creek upsteam. The loop taks you to the Store Point Burial Ground, schoolhouse site and past various old house sites.

g: Walk · 11.6 km return · 4 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · Occassional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This walk takes in most of the Rubicon Heritage Walk, passing through beautiful Mountain Ash forests and sections of cool temperate rainforest, crossing an impressive timber trestle bridge and walking along the aqueduct that feeds the Royston Power Station. It also then loops out to Rubicon Dam and its impressive spillway into Rubicon River. Note: The walk passes alongside an aqueduct, so care should be taken, particularly with children, not to fall into this concrete aqueduct. There are no toilets at the trailhead. Nearest toilets are back at Rubicon Camping Area.
properties.a: From Melbourne, follow the Maroondah Highway. Turn right onto the Taggerty-Thornton Road and right again onto Rubicon Road. Once you drive past the bridge over the Rubicon River, the road name changes to Royston Road. Continue along Royston road for a further 5.7km to the carpark at the start of the walk. Note - this carpark is the starting point for of the Rubicon Heritage Walk also.

g: Walk · 0.8 km return · 30 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · Occassional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: A hidden waterfall nestled in the heart of the Upper Murray, Thowgla Falls is located off Marginal Road in the Thowgla Valley, about 50km south of Corryong. The walk crosses three footbridges through native bushland and ferns on a well-formed track up to a viewing platform with views to the falls.
properties.a: Access Thowgla falls walking track via Thowgla falls day visitor carpark

g: Walk · 2.5 km return · 1.33 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: A beautiful loop walk through tall wet forest and taking in the picturesque riverine environment along the Toorongo and Little Toorongo Rivers. The pathway meanders upwards with formed track interspersed with artisan crafted rock stairs. On the way distant glimpses of the Toorongo Falls give you an appreciation of how steep and tall the 25m falls are. An observation deck takes you up close to the falls where you can hear the water rumbling and see the cascades of water tumbling over the boulders. Continue on the loop trail to take in the Amphitheatre Falls or return back the way you came in if you are short on time. The Amphitheatre loop walk takes you through tall forest to a unique…
properties.a: Head east from Noojee on the Mount Baw Baw Tourist Road for approximately 2km and take a left turn into Toorongo Valley Road. Access to the carpark for the walk is at the end of this 10km well formed gravel road. The walk is sign-posted from the carpark.

g: Mountain bike · 0.6 km return · Easy
properties.d: This circuit trail starting and finishing at the day visitor area is an easy trail suitable for young children and those new to mountain biking. It contains small rollers and berms.

g: Mountain bike · 1.4 km one way · Intermediate
properties.d: This fun filled predominately downhill trail is littered with potential for air time and grin inspiring berms.

g: Mountain bike · 6 km one way · under 1 hr · Intermediate
properties.d: A 6km long single track which starts at the lower trailhead and ends at the upper trailhead. This climbing track has some easy benched in sections and some climbs to raise a sweat. It leads through dense forest and rocky hillsides to ultimately arrive at the top.
properties.a: Located 15 minutes from Bairnsdale. Travel north through Wy Yung and follow the Bullumwaal Rd. The intersection to Mount Taylor is where the bitumen road turns to gravel

g: Mountain bike · 15.5 km return · 1–4 hrs · Intermediate
properties.d: RIDING DIRECTION: Clockwise. Start from the Trail Head with a climb up the first section of the ‘Shack Loop’, cross the fire road and ride down a fun section of trail to No.1 Link Rd. Ride along Willow Tree Rd (dirt road) for two kilometres and then enter back onto single track on the right just past Northern Fire Trail. Ride along an undulating trail to an intersection where you decide whether to test the legs up the steep climb on the left, or take the short cut straight ahead. Have a break then get stuck into the awesome descent back down to the start of Willow Tree Road. Follow your outbound route again and decide which of three trails in the Shack complex to head back down to the…
properties.a: From Yackandandah, drive or ride approximately 4km along Bells Flat Rd and Service Basin Rd (both 2WD gravel roads) and follow the signs to the trailhead next to Yackandandah Creek.

g: Mountain bike · 17 km return · 1–4 hrs · Intermediate
properties.d: RIDING DIRECTION: Clockwise. Start from the Trail Head with a short climb and then out along the nearly flat raceline, watching out for the steep slopes below the trail in some sections. Climb up the next section to a trail intersection, and either keep climbing up to Service Basin Rd to access the fun loop in Bullocky Gully (the longer route), or descend from the intersection down the switchbacks to head more directly back to the Trail head (the shorter route). Intermediate, 1.5 to 2 hours, 17 km
properties.a: From Yackandandah, drive or ride approximately 4km along Bells Flat Rd and Service Basin Rd (both 2WD gravel roads) and follow the signs to the trailhead next to Yackandandah Creek.

g: Mountain bike · 18.5 km return · 1–4 hrs · Intermediate
properties.d: RIDING DIRECTION: Anti-clockwise. Start from the Trail Head with a climb up the first section of the ‘Shack Loop’, cross the road, and begin the long steady climb, which uses sections of old gold mining racelines. Once you reach the top, have a breather, then get set for the flowing seven kilometre descent, before returning to the Trail Head with a winding traverse along mostly old mining racelines. Intermediate, 1.5 to 2 hours, 18.5 km
properties.a: From Yackandandah, drive or ride approximately 4km along Bells Flat Rd and Service Basin Rd (both 2WD gravel roads) and follow the signs to the trailhead next to Yackandandah Creek.

g: Mountain bike · 5 km return · under 1 hr · Intermediate
properties.d: RIDING DIRECTION: Anti-clockwise. This is a compact area with a number of trail options for riders looking to get a feel for Yack Tracks, or for a quick warm-up before hitting the longer loops. Start with the Shack Loop, and when feeling confident to move up to a slightly more technical trail, try the Intermediate rated ‘Boguns Run’ as an alternative return. Note that the ‘Carcass Canyon’ is an even more technical Intermediate rated trail, so have a good look before committing. Intermediate, Under 1 hour, 5 km
properties.a: From Yackandandah, drive or ride approximately 4km along Bells Flat Rd and Service Basin Rd (both 2WD gravel roads) and follow the signs to the trailhead next to Yackandandah Creek.

g: Mountain bike · 18 km one way · Difficult
properties.d: Scaletric Loops is an 18 km MTB track through the Colquhuon Regional Park, it provides a smooth flowing trail with bermed corners, dips, double dips and optional jumps. The Lollipop segment is a fun, fast, descending rollercoaster ride that you won’t forget. It follows the Gippsland Lakes Discovery trail for 1.5 km before climbing back to the trailhead carpark. The trail is well signposted and there are shorter options that can be taken if desired. An 18km cross country mountain bike loop through local forest. This track starts and finishes at the Bruce Rd trailhead.
properties.a: The trail head is on Bruce Rd, 100m from the intersection with the Princes Hwy, approx. 7km from Lakes Entrance.

g: Mountain bike · 4.2 km return · 45 min · Intermediate with Difficult Sections
properties.d: Hey Hey My My mountain bike trail starts near the intersection of Crusher Track and Old Warburton Road. The trail is rated as Blue with Black Diamond “B” lines and begins with a steep 2.5km climb that involves 35 switch back corners and an average gradient of 8%. Once at the top, the fast and flowy single track winds its way down through dry, open heathy forest. The 1.8km descent includes gap jumps, drops, berms and steep sections and finishes at the trailhead on Crusher Track.
properties.a: Access via Crusher Track just off old Warburton Road

g: Mountain bike · 4.3 km one way · 30 min · Easy
properties.d: RIDING DIRECTION: Anti-clockwise. This easy rated green and all abilities trail is a 4.3 km loop that starts and finishes at the Yack Tracks MTB trail head. Start the climb following the green arrows along the epic trail. At the gravel pit carpark after approximately 600 m the trail splits. Adaptive mountain bikes follow the aMTB sign onto Gravel Pit Road for the rest of the ascent. Other mountain bikes can continue along the single track following the green arrows. After the short ascent the tracks re-join. Enjoy flowing decent back to the trailhead through open eucalypt forest Easy - 4.2km - 25 mins - 51m total climb.
properties.a: From the main street of Yackandandah follow Bells Flat Rd for approx. 3km until you meet Service Basin Rd. Continue along Service Basin Rd, which then becomes Yack Gate Rd, for approx. 1.5km to the Yack Tracks MTB Trail Head.

g: Trail bike · 77 km return · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: This loop is mostly a medium grade of difficulty with a few more difficult sections. It comprises of open forest roads and narrow steep and hilly tracks. Some steep sections may become slippery following rain. There are a few creek and river crossings which are usually shallow.
properties.a: To access the Mount Taylor Trail Bike Visitor Area from Bairnsdale, follow the signs to Wy Yung, and then travel north along the Bullumwaal Road for approximately 7km. Turn right onto Boyds Road, follow Boyds Rd. across Mt Taylor Creek and up past a quarry on the left. The trail Bike visitor area is 400m past the quarry. It is immediately past the intersection of Howitt Spur Rd and Jones Rd.

g: Walk · 12 km one way · 1–4 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Gentle hills · Some steps · Limited signage
properties.d: This walk follows an old timber tramline established by William Richard to gain access to the timber in the Starvation Creek valley. The walk starts at the stairs at Big Pats Recreation and Camping Area and first follows Richards Curves Walk to Mississippi Fireline where it continues 9km along the entire tramline length through tall Eucalyptus forests until you reach Brahams Road. Alternatively you can shorten this walk by taking the Richards Tramline Link, this will take you to Mississippi Road. This walking track is one way and can be completed in either direction.
properties.a: From Melbourne head out along the Maroondah Highway to Lilydale. Past Lilydale, head right onto Warburton Highway. Continue the extent of Warburton Highway, through the township of Warburton onto Woods Point Road. Just after you cross the Yarra River about 3km up Wood Point Road take a right turn up Riverside Drive and take your next left up Big Pats Creek Road. Continue along this road through the small settlement of Big Pats Creek until you cross the creek itself, then take your first right just after the bridge up Burns Road. Not far up this road you will reach the Big Pats Recreation Area…

g: Mountain bike · 0.38 km return · under 1 hr · Intermediate
Mountain bike · 9 km one way · under 1 hr · Intermediate
properties.d: Southern Cross Track is a moderate blue square cross country MTB circuit starting at the south east corner of the picnic area, under the tall pine trees. It has one short steep climb before dropping into some fast flowing single track through open forest, crossing some rocky areas and gullies before a fun down hill section parallel to the road before looping back to the picnic area.
properties.a: From Bairnsdale, travel north through Wy Yung and follow the Bullumwaal Rd. The intersection to Mount Taylor is where the bitumen road turns to gravel. It is sign posted "Mt Taylor MTB park".

g: Walk · 3.2 km return · 1 hr · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · No steps · Limited signage

g: Mountain bike · 0.4 km return · under 1 hr · Difficult

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Omeo to Buchan - Cowombat Flat Track
g: 4WD · 8 km return · 1–4 hrs · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with some 4WD experience or training. This seasonal side trip takes you to the entrance of the Cobberas Wilderness Zone. This track is part of the Alpine Walking Track, a 650km track following the ridges and high plains through some of the highest country in Australia.
properties.a: This side track starts over 40km east of Benambra on the Limestone Road, at the intersection of Limestone Road and Cowombat Flat Track.

g: Walk · 0.4 km return · 15 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Many steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This walk crosses a branch of Bentley Creek and passes through tall Mountain Gum Forest A short 500m return walk through the Bentley Plain natural Features and Scenic Reserve. The walk is mostly on boardwalk through tall Mountain Gum forest.
properties.a: The walk starts behind Moscow Villa. Access from Ensay is via Bentleys Plain Road and from Swifts Creek is via Nunniong Road and Bentleys Plain Road.

g: Walk · 10 km return · 3 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Very steep · Many steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Mill track shows a different aspect from the northern side of the Murrindindi Scenic Reserve up to Jacksons road over the bridge to the carpark where it joins up with the Wilhelmina Falls Walk. Descend down the Wilhelmina track and take in the stunning valley views before carefully stepping between and over the granite boulders to the base of the 70 m waterfall. Keep following the track down to the SEC footbridge then back to the Suspension Bridge.
properties.a: From Melbourne - travel along the Melba Highway to the intersection of Murrindindi Road just before Devlins Bridge. Turn right and drive 10km to the Reserve. The Suspension Bridge picnic area is located behind the Rangers Station and the Murrindindi River Walk trailhead can be found over the suspension bridge and to the right.

g: Scenic drive · 48 km return · 4+ hrs · Medium
properties.d: Starting and finishing at Telephone Box Junction, the Circuit Road offers a scenic touring loop around Mt. Stirling. Presenting expansive views of nearby iconic peaks, It also provides access to many attractions including Craig's Hut, Razorback Hut, Howqua Gap Hut and Bindaree Falls. It is also an entry point for 4x4 and camping trips in the high country
properties.a: From Mansfield follow the Mt. Buller Rd to Mirimbah. Turn left onto Mt. Stirling Rd and follow to Telephone Box Junction (T.B.J). From here, The Circuit Road can be driven in either direction. There is information/map boards at T.B.J and Circuit Rd Picnic Area. The drive is normally accessible to all vehicles, but can have rough sections. The Circuit Road is seasonally closed at T.B.J from the Friday before the Queen's Birthday weekend until the Thursday before the Melbourne Cup Weekend.

g: Mountain bike · 1.7 km one way · Intermediate
properties.d: This climbing trail contains a number of tight climbing switch backs and offers great views.

g: Walk · 2.5 km return · 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Many steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This walk meanders through Alpine Ash Forest and Riparian Thicket. A 2.2 km loop walk through the Bentley Plain Natural Features and Scenic Reserve highlighting the beautiful Alpine Ash forest.
properties.a: The track starts behind Moscow Villa. Access is via Ensay and Bentleys Plain Road from the south or Swifts Creek and Nunniong Road from the north.

properties.n: Aberfeldy Backroad Tour - Donnellys Creek Loop -White Star Township
g: 4WD · 21.4 km return · 30 min · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. This side trip takes you to the township site of White Star, which sprang up after the discovery of quartz by good natured Welshman, Jack Middleton, known for his generosity within the area. En route to White Star is The Germans, Mt Pleasant Hotel Site as well as Smith’s Hotel site with a short walk into the lone grave of William Watts.The Mt Pleasant Hotel site (1864 – 1869) was run by the Crooks family. Mr Crooks was not favourable within the community, having a reputation for his kleptomaniac tendencies – Mr Crooks was a crook!
properties.a: At the intersection of Donnellys Creek Road and Springs Road, continue north along Springs Road until you get to White Star Track. Turn left onto White Star Track and follow until you get to White Star Mine Track. Follow White Star Mine Track to the historical White Star township site.

g: Mountain bike · 3.5 km return · under 1 hr · Intermediate
properties.d: A 3.5km single track which begins in the north east corner of the Mt Taylor picnic area. It crosses a gully and up the forest road for 100m before turning right steeply up the past two old mine shafts and onto a spur. A few TTF's are crossed then several hundred metres through bush and back down the forest road again. it follows Leadoux Track heading quickly into a gully then swings back along the base of a rock slab, through tight and tricky rock sections. Milky Way Track crosses Flow Track and joins the lower 500m of the All Mountain and Downhill Track returning to the lower trailhead.
properties.a: From Bairnsdale, travel north through Wy Yung and follow the Bullumwaal Rd. The intersection to Mount Taylor is where the bitumen road turns to gravel. It is sign posted "Mt Taylor MTB park".

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Briagolong to Dargo - Lees Creek
g: 4WD · 5.8 km return · 1–4 hrs · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with some 4WD experience or training. This side trip is a short drive to Lees Creek Picnic Area, where you can enjoy a picnic at the junction of Freestone and Lees Creek or stretch your legs on the 4km Alistair Fielding Loop Walk. The multi-day Track Ninety Six Walk also passes through this picnic area.
properties.a: About 4km past Lloyds Knob campground, turn off Freestone Creek Road, down Lees Creek Track.

g: Walk · 1.1 km return · 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Well formed trk · Short steep hills · Occassional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: A short, steep pleasant walk rewards walkers with spectacular granite boulder formations and views over the Strathbogies. Access onto the top of a large granite boulder is possible at the top end of this walk but if venturing onto its top, please exercise caution, particularly with children, as there are no safety railings and steep drop-offs. A short, steep pleasant walk rewards walkers with spectacular granite boulder formations a renowned feature of the Strathbogies.
properties.a: The walk can be accessed from Lima East Day Visitor carpark or from James Reserve campground.

g: Walk · 0.4 km return · 30 min · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Gentle hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Meringtons Walk follows the route to the gravesite of Charles Brown near the Meringtons Campground. The majority of the track is well maintained and clearly defined, but access to the grave requires wading through the Aberfeldy River. River depths vary per season so proceed with caution when crossing the river.

g: Walk · 0.14 km return · under 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · Many steps · Sign posted
properties.d: While exploring the old Red Jacket township site, make sure you visit the old cemetery site. The short walk climbs from the town centre into the cemetery. Explore the gravestones of the people that once lived in this mining ghost town.

g: Walk · 5 km return · 1 hr · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · Occasional steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: A peaceful walk along a well maintained track that follows a 2.5km section of an historic timber tramway once used to haul logs out of the forest. Starting opposite the Noojee DELWP depot in the Day Visitor Area carpark, the walk immediately takes you up close to some old timber tramway relics and interpretative signs. Continue up a gentle incline through beautiful tall forests, where you may see lyrebirds, parrots or even a deer. You will pass through an occasional small gully where a tramway bridge would once have stood, but is now covered in a thick under story of tall ferns enveloping the track. The trail ends at a beautiful spot on the Loch River where there are picnic tables…
properties.a: Head north on Bennett Street from the Noojee township across the bridge over the Latrobe River. Take the left turn immediately after the bridge into McCarthy Spur Road. Follow this road across a second bridge over the Loch River where you will find parking at the picnic ground on your left.

properties.n: Aberfeldy Backroad Tour - Donnellys Creek Loop - Alternative start via Seaton
g: 4WD · 21.5 km one way · 50 min · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. This route is an alternative state for the Donnellys Creek Tour, starting at Seaton instead of Walhalla. It goes over Murderers Hill and passes through a number of historic sites along McEvoys Track. McEvoys Track has a long and rich history, dating back to before 1862. Around this time, a public meeting was held in Sale and a reward of 50 pounds was offered for the discovery of the best track to the Jordan River diggings. Tom McEvoy and Portugee Joe’s Track was deemed to be the best route, commencing at Seaton, climbing the ridge with the Thomson Watershed on the left and the Glenmaggie Creek on the right,…
properties.a: This route is an alternative starting point for the Donnellys Creek Tour. Commencing at the Seaton-Glenmaggie Road intersection with McEvoys Track, head north-west on McEvoys Track. Continue along McEvoys Track and onto Springs Road (same road) to join the Donnellys Creek Tour further on.

g: Walk · 8.5 km one way · 1–4 hrs
properties.d: 3.7km one-way walking track that runs from Mt Buller to Mirimbah or vice versa. The altitude of the track rises 1000m from bottom to top with steep and remote sections, it's suitable for experienced bushwalkers.
properties.a: From Mt Buller, the track starts from a timber shelter opposite the Arlberg Hotel. Follow the nature walk to Spurs Restaurant then down the road along Burnt Hut Ski Run, then veer left onto the walking track at the Bonza Ski Lift. From Mirimbah the track starts from the carpark opposite Mirimbah park.

g: Walk · 0.84 km one way · 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Well formed track · Very steep · No steps · No directional signage
properties.d: Get glimpses over Goughs Bay and the Delatite Arm through the newly regenerated surrounding forest. This site was once a pine plantation and has since been revegetated with forest species to the area. A steep track takes you up to the peak at the top, a walk often used by local residents of Goughs Bay.
properties.a: Located on the far side of Goughs Bay. Take Mansfield-Woods Point Rd, turn onto Piries-Goughs Bay Rd. Drive through Goughs Bay on Bayside Boulevard wich turns in to Frys Bay Road (2WD Dirt Road). The start of the walking track is located at the start of Frys Bay road, however if you continue to drive there are other access point to the walk

g: Walk · 1.6 km return · 30 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This walking track runs along the river corridor from the Toorongo Falls campgrounds up to the Toorongo Falls Picnic Area. From there you can link up for a longer walk to the Toorongo Falls Walk, to view the falls

g: Walk · 0.6 km return · 30 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · Many steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: This walk starts across the road from the Cascades Picnic Area. The walk drops down through the forested valley to the Murrindindi River, via a track and a series of steps and stairs. Two bridges span the river, giving you views of the river as it cascades down a rocky face. Enjoy the view and then retrace your steps back up to the Cascades Picnic Area.
properties.a: From Melbourne - Travel along the Melba Highway to the intersection of Murrindindi Road just before Devlins Bridge. Turn right and drive 10km to the Reserve then follow the Murrindindi Road south for approximately 9km past the Rangers Hut to the Cascades Picnic Area on the right hand side. The Cascades walk starts across the road from the picnic area.

g: Walk · 1.6 km one way · 1–4 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This trail is an extension of the Plain Creek Loop walk, taking you to the remains of the old timber trestle bridge once part of the tramway used to transport fallen timber. Carter & Co. built a sawmill in this area in 1937 to mill timber from the surrounding forest. In the early years timber was transported through the forest by a single line five horse team along timber tramways as seen in this walk.
properties.a: From Mansfield follow the Mt. Buller Rd to Sawmill Settlement, turn left onto Carters Rd

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Briagolong to Dargo
g: 4WD · 73 km one way · 4+ hrs · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. The Briagolong-Dargo scenic drive is a beautiful half-day journey along Freestone Creek, with opportunities for bushwalks and picnicking. You may also choose to make this an overnight trip with some overnight stays at one of several camping sites along this route, which would enable you to explore some of the bushwalks in this area. One of the highlights of this trip is Blue Pool, where visitors can cool off in the swimming hole or take one of several walks which depart from the day visitor area. Starting in Briagolong, travel north along Forbes Street which becomes Freestone Creek Road, and stay on it until…
properties.a: Start in Briagolong, travelling north along Forbes Street which becomes Freestone Creek Road, and continue on to reach Blue Pool.

g: Walk · 4.2 km return · 2 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occassional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This walk takes you to the historic Morning Star waterwheel and mining relics of the Crinoline township. The walking track start off Middle Star Track. Across a narrow bridge you will find an undulating walk with some steeper rocky sections. Past the Morning Star Mine the walk can be extended onward to the Crinoline battery built in the gold mining days to service the Morning Star Gold Mine.
properties.a: Access to the Morning Star Walk is via Donnellys Creek Rd (Aberfeldy backroads tour.) From here turn onto Middle Start Track and you will find the trailhead on the right just before crossing Donellys Creek.

g: Trail bike · 84 km return · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: A medium grade of difficulty, with a few more difficult sections, this loop comprises open forest roads and narrow steep and hilly tracks. Some sections are not maintained and have overgrown vegetation and intersections may not be obvious. Some steep sections may become slippery following rain. There are a few creek and river crossings which are usually shallow.
properties.a: To access the Mount Taylor Trail Bike Visitor Area from Bairnsdale, follow the signs to Wy Yung, and then travel north along the Bullumwaal Road for approximately 7km. Turn right onto Boyds Road, follow Boyds Rd. across Mt Taylor Creek and up past a quarry on the left. The trail Bike visitor area is 400m past the quarry. It is immediately past the intersection of Howitt Spur Rd and Jones Rd.

g: Walk · 1.6 km return · 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Steepish but short walk up to the lookout over Bright. A short climb through native forest for a great view of Bright from the lookout.
properties.a: Walk or drive approx. 1km from the centre of Bright up Deacon Ave, and park in Zivan Crt. Walk up the short access track to the start of the walking track. Alternatively, walk 250m up the 4WD track from McFadyens Lane.

g: Mountain bike · 0.6 km one way · Difficult
properties.d: This old school hand-built trail drops steeply off Acheron Ridge straight to the car park, avoiding Spider Gully. It is skinny, steep, rocky and off camber with many exposed roots.

g: Walk · 3.6 km return · 1.5 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Gentle hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: The Ada Tree Walk meanders its way through cool temperate rainforest with groves of Sassafras, ancient Myrtle Beech and tree ferns towards a viewing platform at the Ada Tree, a giant Mountain Ash considered to be one of Victoria's largest trees. The Ada Tree can be reached from the Ada Tree car park via the walking track that meanders through the Island Creek rainforest. Inexperienced walkers may find this walk slightly challenging due to some uneven sections and natural steps. The walk is 3.2km and a 1.5 hour walk return trip from the car park and picnic area. Whilst walking notice the variety of tree species and the changes of structure along the walk. The feature of this walk is the Ada…
properties.a: From Powelltown, head east along the Yarra Junction - Noojee Road (C425) for 6km then turn left up Big Creek Road. Travel along Big Creek Road for 22km and turn right down Federal Road. Travel along Federal Road for 3km until you reach the Ada Tree Picnic Area. From Warburton Travel along the Warburton - Woodspoint Road (C511) for 10km and Turn Right onto Brahams Road. Continue for 13km and veer left onto Big Creek Road. After 4km, turn right down Federal Road. Travel along Federal Road for 3km until you reach the Ada Tree Picnic Area. For Disabled Access: A key is available at the Powelltown…

g: Walk · 1.6 km return · 1 hr · Grade 4
properties.t: Rough many obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: A steep four-wheel drive track leads to the start of this walk. Numerous relics including chimneys, hut sites and diggings from an early mining settlement reward the walker.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Bairnsdale to Dargo - Angusvale
g: 4WD · 33 km return · 1–4 hrs · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. This side trip off the main High Country Backroad Tour - Bairnsdale to Dargo Tour heads down to Angusvale, a very popular campground along the banks of the Mitchell River. Pause at Angusvale Lookout for views of Tabberabbera Nature Conservation Reserve and Angusvale, before continuing on another 2.6kms to Angusvale Camping Area. Mitchell River is the largest free flowing river in Victoria. To help protect the fragile Heritage River environment, camping is not permitted within 50 metres of the water.
properties.a: Turn off the Bairnsdale-Dargo Road, down the Mitchell River Road to Angusvale.

g: Horse riding · 24 km return · overnight · Advanced
Walk · 24 km return · 8 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occassional steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: This trail follows the forests and meandering course of the Jamieson River, linking the Grannys Flat Camping Reserve to Mitchells Flat, and is considered an advanced ride. The trail follows the forests and meandering course of the Jamieson River, linking the Grannys Flat Camping Reserve to Mitchells Flat. Tree species commonly seen along the riverbanks are characteristic of Australian dry foothill forests and valleys, including Manna Gum, Broad-leaved Peppermint, Blue Gum and Stringybark species. Along the Bridle track there are two sites of historical significance, the remnants of the Quicksilver mercury mine and the dwellings of the Mitchell and Hoskins families at Mitchells Flat.
properties.a: Follow the Mount Buller Road from Mansfield towards Merrijig for 4 km. Turn right at the sign for Jamieson and travel for 35 km. Turn left at the Heyfield (Licola) - Jamieson Road in Jamieson. After 7.5 km on this gravel road you will reach the Granny’s Flat Camping Reserve sign on your left. The campsite is down 1 km of windy road. This road is steep, but is accessible to all traffic, except after heavy rain, when it may become temporarily inaccessible to 2WD’s.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Swifts Creek to Buchan
g: 4WD · 75 km one way · 1–4 hrs · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. An easy half day trip between the Tambo and Snowy catchments. In the dry this is a great shortcut and alternative to following the highway between these two communities. With views into the Mt Elizabeth Nature Conservation Reserve this drive has you crossing over the Timbarra River before heading into Buchan. Consider a visit to the Buchan Caves Reserve to explore Victoria’s largest cave system or even do one of the other 4WD tours which connect to this town. The tour begins in Swifts Creek heading south on the Great Alpine Road for 16.6km then turning left at Ensay onto Horsefall Street/Little River Road and…
properties.a: Starting from the main street of Swifts Creek, head south on the Great Alpine Road. Drive with care as stock may be on roads.

properties.n: Aberfeldy Backroad Tour - Woods Point to Jamieson - Macks Creek
g: 4WD · 3.2 km return · 1 hr · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with some 4WD experience or training. This side trip takes you up a 4WD track to a short 500m return walk to the old Macks Creek settlement site. The settlement was surveyed in 1865 and named the ‘Township of Kevington at Macks Creek’. It boasted 22 buildings and a post office.
properties.a: This side trip is accessed off the Mansfield – Woods Point Road, heading south on a forest track on the western edge of Kevington.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Omeo to Dargo - Harrisons Cut
g: 4WD · 21 km return · 1–4 hrs · Difficult (Black Diamond)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with reasonable 4WD experience or 4WD training. This optional side trip off continues up to the hidden end of the Upper Dargo Road to Harrisons Cut, a fifty-metre channel blasted through the rock to divert the Dargo River, to enable the river to be mined for gold in the early 1880s. On your way to Harrisons Cut, you will pass opportunities for bush camping by the Dargo River at Black Flat and Collins Flat.
properties.a: This side trip commences from the Upper Dargo Road/Jones Road intersection, heading north up Upper Dargo Road with the Dargo River on your right

g: Mountain bike · 5.9 km one way · under 1 hr · Intermediate
properties.d: This is a descending cross-country track with log ramps and dirt humps/jumps. This track is also good to use for climbing from the carpark trailhead to the top.
properties.a: Nowa Nowa MTB Park is located on the Nowa Nowa - Buchan Rd, approx. 1.5 km from Nowa Nowa township.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Timbarra Loop
g: 4WD · 124 km return · 4 hrs · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with some 4WD experience or training. Timbarra Loop is a leisurely drive exploring the Timbarra River in the upper reaches of the Tambo catchment, passing well-known campsites and good fishing opportunities along both Timbarra and Buchan Rivers. The loop starts from Buchan heading north on the Gelantipy Road for 20km to W Tree Falls. This viewing area on the Gelantipy Road offers great views of W Tree Falls and its watercourse, which flows into the Snowy River via the Murrindal and Buchan Rivers. Continue on Gelantipy Road and at Gelantipy turn left on to Glenmore Road towards Glenmore Camp - a great open picnic stop or campsite on the flats on the Buchan River with…
properties.a: Starting at Buchan and heading north on Gelantipy Road. This tour does require the crossing of the Buchan River which can vary in flow and depth – Ensure you are appropriately equipped before tackling this.

g: Scenic drive · 11 km return · under 1 hr · Easy
properties.d: This drive starts to the south of Marysville township and continues along Paradise Plains road past the Marysville water reservoir to take in some spectacular views of Marysville and the surrounding valley. Park at the Keppel lookout carpark and walk the short distance to the lookout. Be sure to have your camera with you as you will be impressed with the panoramic views.
properties.a: From Marysville’s main street, turn south at the roundabout up Lyell St and continue onto Paradise Plains Rd, past the town reservoir (1.4km). Mopoke View looks out over the valley to the south of Marysville (4km). At the top of the climb, turn left onto Keppel Lookout Rd (4.7km) and continue until you reach the carpark (5.5km) at Keppels Lookout.

g: Walk · 0.7 km one way · under 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Very steep · No steps · Limited signage
properties.d: This walking track is accessible from Richards Tramline and provides a link between Richard Tramline and Mississippi Road cutting the otherwise 9km walk to Brahams Road a few kilometres shorter to Mississippi Road. For the majority of the track it follows Mississippi Creek where you can see. The Richards tramline network is one way and can be completed in either direction. For further information please see 'Richards Tramline'.
properties.a: From Melbourne head out along the Maroondah Highway to Lilydale. Past Lilydale, head right onto Warburton Highway. Continue the extent of Warburton Highway, through the township of Warburton onto Woods Point Road. Just after you cross the Yarra River about 3km up Wood Point Road take a right turn up Riverside Drive and take your next left up Big Pats Creek Road. Continue along this road through the small settlement of Big Pats Creek until you cross the creek itself, then take your first right just after the bridge up Burns Road. Not far up this road you will reach the Big Pats Recreation Area…

properties.n: Link track between picnic area and campground
g: Walk · 0.25 km one way · 6 min · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Well formed trk · Flat · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: This track provides pedestrian access between the day visitor area and the camping area.

g: Mountain bike · 5.7 km one way · under 1 hr · Difficult
properties.d: This is a descending cross-country track with several earth and log ramps. Track 3 meanders a bit further afield crossing the power line easement with multiple switchbacks and eventually joining the bottom section of Track 2.
properties.a: Nowa Nowa MTB Park is located on the Nowa Nowa - Buchan Rd, approx. 1.5 km from Nowa Nowa township.

g: Mountain bike · 0.35 km return · under 1 hr · Easy
properties.d: Loop ride suitable for beginners

g: Mountain bike · 6.1 km return · under 1 hr · Easy
Walk · 6.1 km return · 2 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Limited signage
properties.d: Starting at The Boys Camp, this 6.1 km return loop takes in both sides of the Rubicon River. The trail meanders along the river for a large part of the walk which is perfect for taking in the sounds of the river, the birds and the rustling trees. Cross the bridge over the pipeline and follow the road towards Camp Jungai and back onto the trail. The remainder of the trail passes through the bush above the campgroundsbefore ending back at The Boys Camp. A popular relatively easy looping track dipping into the gully along the picturesque Rubicon Rivers waters edge and then back up the sloping banks over boardwalk and bridges. A multi purpose trail that winds through the Rubicon Valley on both…
properties.a: From Melbourne, follow the Maroondah Highway; turn right onto the Taggerty-Thornton road and right again onto Rubicon road. Starting and looping back to finish at The Boys Camp the trail is located 6.5km along Rubicon Road.

g: 4WD · 28 km one way · 4 hrs · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: This 4WD tour runs between the Avon-Mt Hedrick Scenic Reserve and State forest that joins the Avon Wilderness and the Alpine National Park to the north. It takes in a number of scenic lookouts and involves a couple of river crossings. A scenic 4WD tour through the Avon-Mt Hedrick scenic reserve.
properties.a: The 4WD tour starts on Kentucky Rd in Maffra West Upper. Follow Kentucky Rd north, turning left onto Huggetts Trk at the roads end. Follow Huggetts Trk through, turning right onto Mt Angus Trk. Finish the tour by turning right onto Okeefe Rd and you will finish at the Wombat Crossing campgrounds.

g: Mountain bike · 0.3 km one way · Intermediate
properties.d: This trail creates a short-cut removing the last climb and descent gully on Acheron Ridge. The trail is named after a fox that watched from a safe distance during construction.

g: Walk · 1.55 km one way · under 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Well formed track · Gentle hills · Occasional steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: Stop in at the Stringybark Creek Historic Reserve to get your dose of local history. This is the spot that the infamous Kelly gang shot and killed three police officers (Constables Lonigan, Scanlan and sergent Kennedy) in 1878. This track visits the key sites of this event, with on-site information signs detailing the events of those times. Step back in time and take the Stringybark Creek Loop Walk that re-enacts the path that Constable McIntyre and Sergeant Kennedy took as they tried to escape from the Kelly gang. The walk is 1400 metres in length and takes approximately 40 minutes to complete with the occasional steps.
properties.a: From Benalla head south on Benalla-Tatong Road (C517), go through the small town of Tatong and after about 27km turn right onto Stringybark Creek Road.

g: Walk · 3.4 km return · 2 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: A steady climb above Bright through quiet eucalypt forest. Return the same way. Walk up around the side of the hill through native forest, with glimpses of Bright and the Ovens Valley through the trees.
properties.a: Valley View Walking track begins from the first bend in Hargreaves Road. If driving, park on Sommer Ave and follow the roadsigns up Hargreaves Road for 200m to the start of the walking track.

properties.n: Aberfeldy Backroad Tour - Woods Point to Jamieson - German Spur Track
g: 4WD · 14 km one way · 1–4 hrs · Difficult (Black Diamond)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with reasonable 4WD experience or 4WD training. This side trip is a difficult 4WD alternative to travelling along the Woods Point-Jamieson Road, with short rocky sections and a long steep decline where it joins up with the main road just south of Knockwood. This difficult 4WD track takes you past German Spur Settlement and the Alpine Hotel. In the late 1800s this was the original track to Woods Point from the north. German Spur Track was used to detour around Gaffneys Creek to access the Upper Goulburn diggings more directly. The track was likely named after Charles Yukert who operated the German Alpine Hotel. The site of this hotel, which burnt down in 1865 when the…
properties.a: This side trip is accessed off the Mansfield – Woods point Road and heads up German Spur Track.

g: Walk · 0.22 km return · under 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · Occassional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This track links the Stringybark Camping Area with the start of the Stringybark Creek Historic Loop Walk. Take the short walk from the day visitor area to Stringybark campground.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Nunniong Forest Drive
g: 4WD · 86 km return · 4 hrs · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. This leisurely forest drive winds you deep into the heart of Bentley Plains. There are many historic sites and relics along the way, including the iconic Washington Winch, Moscow Villa and Bush Hilton hut. There are several walks as well as camping and picnic facilities near Moscow Villa and Bentley Plain Campgrounds. Start your adventure from Swift Creek, heading south onto Great Alpine Rd, and then turn left onto Horsfall St/Little River Rd. Continue on to eventually turn right onto Bently Plain Rd, which will lead you to Bently Plains—a sub-alpine grassland and wet heathland rich in unique flora species.…
properties.a: The drive starts in Swift Creek, heading south onto Great Alpine Rd, and then turning left onto Horsfall St/Little River Rd.

properties.n: Aberfeldy Backroad Tour - Jordan Valley - Aberfeldy Crossing
g: 4WD · 6 km return · 14 min · Difficult (Black Diamond)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with reasonable 4WD experience or 4WD training. This side trip down O’Keefe Track takes you down to the start of a 300m walking track which leads into Aberfeldy Crossing. Here interpretation material explains the history of the area and the previous residents who lived here, including Thomas Fawkner, Thomas Theobold, Sarah Matthews and William ‘Billy the cook’ Bryant.
