properties.a: Side trip commences down O’Keefe Track, which is about 1.8km north of Aberfeldy, off the Walhalla Road. This side trip concludes at the intersection of O'Keefe Track and O'Keefe McGuire Link Track. From here the walking track takes you to Aberfeldy Crossing.

g: Walk · 0.8 km one way · 30 min · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Formed track · Flat · No steps · Limited signage
properties.d: The Middle Red Gums Walk cuts through the centre of the North block. This gets you further away from the access roads and provides a good example of the plains grassy woodland environment.
properties.a: The Briagolong Red Gum Reserve is located just South of the township of Briagolong on the East side of the Briagolong Road. A picnic area with information shelter is located on the North side of O’Connor Road which cuts through the centre of the reserve. The Middle Red Gums Walk begins here and comes out onto the North loop at the top of Smith Street in Briagolong.

g: Mountain bike · 2.8 km return · Intermediate
properties.d: This trail starts and finishes in the same place on Acheron Ridge. With a fun filled steep start and a tight switchback climb, this trail adds a challenging extension to your ride.

g: Mountain bike · 0.5 km return · under 1 hr · Easy
Walk · 4.2 km return · 3 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Rough many obstacles · Very steep · Occasional steps · Limited signage
properties.d: Mt Torbreck Summit Walk begins from the Barnewall Plains visitor area on Barnewall Plains road rising to an altitude of 1516m. The track climbs in an easterly and then south easterly direction, getting steeper around the area where the predominant trees change from woolly butt to snow gum. The track is fairly well defined and orange metal triangles attached to trees make route finding fairly easy, even in winter when the track is covered in snow. Views from around the summit are breathtaking on a clear day and well worth the long climb. A rock cairn marks the summit location.
properties.a: From nearby Thornton, follow the Goulburn Valley Highway B 340 to the Snobs Creek pub, 5km before Eildon. Turn right on to Snobs Creek road and drive south for 14 km. Turn right into Barnwell Plains road and continue on for 6 km. Note that the Barnewall Plains road is closed between the Queen's Birthday weekend and Melbourne Cup weekend.

cl.d: The road to access the trailhead (Barnewall Plains Road) is closed between the Queen's Birthday weekend and Melbourne Cup weekend but can still be accessed via a 10 minute walk along the closed road - No vehicle access.

g: Mountain bike · 0.25 km return · under 1 hr · Easy
Walk · 1.1 km return · 30 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Gentle hills · Occasional steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: The track makes a loop around the upper dam that was built in 1916 to provide a permanent supply of water to the town and railway station. It no longer provides water to Bright but offers a short walk close to Bright. Combine with lower loop for a longer walk.

g: Walk · 0.5 km return · 30 min · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Well formed trk · Gentle hills · Occassional steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: The Kalatha Giant Tree Walk is a short easy return trail that takes in the magnificent Kalatha Giant. Thought to be over 350 years old, the large Mountain Ash tree is 73m tall with a girth of 16m. This picturesque trail meanders through beautiful tree ferns, Mountain Pepper and wattles and under some spectacular tall trees. Take the time to read the informative interpretation signs, giving you a greater understanding into the history and ecology of the area. Well worth a visit, the Kalatha Giant Tree Walk is located in the heart of Toolangi State Forest Marvel at the majestic Kalatha tree then continue on the looped track to take in the beauty of the Mountain Ash forest.
properties.a: From Healesville, take the Myers Creek road for 13km. Turn right into Sylvia Creek road and continue on this well maintained forest road for 10km. Kalatha road is on your left. Approximately 2kms down Kalatha road you will see the trailhead for the walk and a small car parking area.

g: Walk · 2.8 km return · 1.25 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: The La La Falls walking track follows the old Four Mile Creek timber tramway for much of its length and is an enjoyable walk beneath a Grey Gum and Mountain Ash canopy. This walk may be challenging for some, as it continues up-hill to the small, yet picturesque falls. The walk also features three unique, hand crafted stone bridges and viewing platform.
properties.a: From Melbourne, travel east along the Maroondah Highway to Lilydale. Beyond Lilydale, turn right onto the Warburton Highway. At the township of Warburton, turn right into Park Road, then left onto La La Avenue shortly after. Signage is present at the entrance to the site at Irruka Road. Alternatively, you can visit the Water Wheel Tourist Information Centre at Warburton for information on other local walks in this area (open 10am-4pm daily).

properties.n: Aberfeldy Backroad Tour - Woods Point to Jamieson - Mountain Home Hotel
g: 4WD · 6 km one way · under 1 hr · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with some 4WD experience or training. Just out of Woods Point you can take the Old Coast Road turnoff just before Jack Scotts Reserve as an optional side trip (Grade – Medium) to the main Woods Point to Jamieson Tour. This side trip passes by the sites of the Barretts Mountain Home Hotel, Charles Brothers Sawmill and Frenchmans Hotel. Onsite interpretation along the route tells some of the history of the gold mining era. In the late 1800s, this was the original track to Woods Point from the north.
properties.a: This side trip is accessed off the Mansfield – Woods Point Road just west of Woods Point and heads north up Old Coast Road.

g: Walk · 0.4 km return · 30 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · Many steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Take a short walk to Bindaree Falls, located in a tranquil setting you will be surrounded by lush native forest and magnificent tree ferns. A wooden viewing platform passes around the back of Bindaree Falls giving you the ability to view the cascading water from the rocks above. This walk is on a well formed track and has some sections of rock steps.
properties.a: From Mansfield follow the Mt. Buller Rd to Mirimbah. Turn left onto Mt. Stirling Rd and follow to Telephone Box Junction (T.B.J). From here, The Circuit Road can be driven in either direction. Follow Circuit Road for 18kms in an anti-clockwise direction, or 28kms in a clockwise direction. Turn onto Bindaree Rd and follow for 5kms. The drive is normally accessible to all vehicles, but can have rough sections. Bindaree Rd is seasonally closed from the Thursday after the Queen's Birthday weekend until the Thursday before the Melbourne Cup Weekend.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Nunniong Forest Drive - Nunniong Plains
g: 4WD · 31 km return · 1–4 hrs · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with some 4WD experience or training. This side trip crosses the Timbarra River, passes by The Culverts and onwards into the Nunniong Plains. The Nunniong Plains are a series of open plains interspersed with Snow Gum Woodlands and stands of Alpine Ash. Camping is available at Nunniong Plains campground near the headwaters of Timbarra River. At times, cattle and feral horses graze these plains.
properties.a: At the western end of Bentley Plain Road, turn right onto Nunniong Road and travel 13.2 kms to then turn right onto Nunniong Plains Track.

g: Walk · 2.5 km one way · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · No steps · Limited signage
properties.d: The New Federal Mill walking track can be a experienced as a detour to the Ada Tree, and leads you the historical Federal Mill site. The walking track moves through Wet Forest type under a canopy of the towering Mountain Ash species, the Tallest Flowering plant in the world. As you approach the Mill, you may notice escapee garden plants such as English Ivy and lilies, which once featured in gardens prepared by Mill workers and their families.
properties.a: The New Federal Mill walking track can only be reached via foot from the Ada Tree Walk along Federal Road or from the Walk into History. By vehicle, take directions to the Ada Tree Picnic Area. Once there, walk along Federal Road for approximately 1km then turn left, following signage to the New Federal Mill site. After 1km, you will reach the historical mill site. At this point, you can retrace your steps back to the Ada Tree Picnic Area or continue along the Walk Into History heading north for approximately 1.6km to rejoin the Ada Tree Walk loop and back to the car park. The New Federal…

g: Walk · 5 km return · 2 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Rough many obstacles · Short steep hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Elevator Walking track is a 5 km return which starts at the lower trailhead of the Mt Taylor mountain bike park. It is signposted from the lower trailhead and heads uphill on a narrow winding track. The track runs parallel to Lookout Rd for a bit over 1 km then crosses the road. It follows a steep boundary track for 400m then into bushy rocky terrain climbing steeply up to more open forest near to Tower Rd. The track passes near to the upper trailhead and does a short loop before re-joining the track. Follow the track back down the same way returning to the beginning.
properties.a: Bairnsdale is approximately 275km east of Melbourne on the Princes Highway. The Elevator walking track is located at Mount Taylor mountain bike park. Follow the signs to Wy Yung. Mt Taylor mountain bike park is 13.5km past Wy Yung hotel. Head north along Bullumwaal Rd. At the point where the bitumen turns to gravel, the mountain bike park/picnic area can be accessed via Lookout Rd, the gravel road on your left.

g: Walk · 0.8 km return · 30 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · Occassional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This walk starts from the picnic area and heads down through the forest and along the Latrobe River. The walk ends in an open grassy area by the river. Relax by the river and when ready, retrace your steps back to the Latrobe River Picnic and Camping Area.
properties.a: This walk starts from the Latrobe River Picnic and Camping Area which is located approximately 90 kilometres east of Melbourne. Turn left just 500m up Ada River Road which is located between the towns of Powelltown and Noojee along the Yarra Junction - Noojee road. With the exception of Ada River Road and the campsite itself, access is entirely on sealed roads from Melbourne as well as from the east, if heading from East Gippsland.

g: Mountain bike
Walk · 1.4 km return · 30 min · Grade 2.1
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: Following the Yackandandah Creek, this shared use trail meanders through open eucalypt foothill forest. See remnants of the areas mining heritage, or spy a platypus in the creek as you enjoy this gentle walk or ride. This trail also forms part of the return loop for the Green Loop mountain bike trail.
properties.a: From the main street of Yackandandah follow Bells Flat Rd for approx. 3km until you meet Service Basin Rd. Continue along Service Basin Rd, which then becomes Yack Gate Rd, for approx. 1.5km to Yack Tracks MTB trail head. The track starts from the carpark.

g: Walk · 1.2 km return · under 1 hr
properties.d: Located on the banks of the Aberfeldy River, 'Hanging Rock' was a particularly popular picnic spot in the late 1800's / early 1900's and was previously situated along a pack track which travelled from Code's Flat to Cullen's Farm and then up to the town of Aberfeldy.
properties.a: Travelling from the Matlock direction (north), turn left into Cullen's Tk. At the 2km mark, veer right onto Comet Spur Tk which is a steeply rutted track - traverse in dry weather only. Travel a further 1.8km before turning left onto Eaton Tk. Travel 800m to the start of the Hanging Rock Walking Track.

g: Walk · 0.9 km return
properties.d: The Crinoline Walk starts past the Morning Star Mine the walk and continues on to the Crinoline battery built in the gold mining days to service the Morning Star Gold Mine

g: Mountain bike · 4.8 km return · under 1 hr · Easy
Walk · 2.3 km return · under 1 hr · Grade 2.1
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Gentle hills · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: A 2.3 km one-way undulating forest walk on a gravel surface through Limestone Box Forest that ends at the Log Crossing Picnic Area.
properties.a: Car parking is available at either end of the track - at the Forestec campus on the Princes Highway, or at Log Crossing, which is 2km from the campus via Uncles Rd.

g: Walk · 2.5 km return · 45 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: A 3km walk through local forest that passes through undulating forest and crosses gullies and forest roads. The walk passes passes by an old concrete magazine which was once used for storing explosives for road building.
properties.a: Access is via the Great Alpine Rd approx 2km from Bruthen township.

g: Walk · 4.4 km return · 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Limited signage
properties.d: This walk takes you back to the Lees Creek alluvial gold mining era of the 1890s where you will be able to view old house sites, alluvial diggings and a water race used to bring water from a dam to the diggings. Nature also abounds with lyrebirds, giant Mountain Grey Gums (Eucalyptus cypellocarpa), tree ferns and maybe the Fringed Helmeted Orchid (Corybas diemenicus) with its bright red flower along the way. Alistair Fielding was a park ranger from Briagolong who had a hope to open up the intriguing history of this area. This was achieved after he passed away and the track now takes off from the pleasant Lee Creek Picnic Area near the junction of Freestone and Lee Creek. The portion of…
properties.a: This track can be accessed from Briagolong by travelling around 30km or 45minutes on the rough 2wd route of Freestone Creek Rd and then around 3km or 10 minutes along the 4wd route of Lee Creek Track to The Lee Creek Picnic Area. Alternatively you can walk to the track from the Lee Creek Camping area which is located on the intersection of Freestone Creek Rd and Lee Creek Track.

g: Walk · 3.1 km return · 1.5 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Gentle hills · Occasional steps · Limited signage
properties.d: This track offers a base level walk starting from the Mitta Mitta Historic Reserve winding through forest and traversing Deep Gully with its temperate rainforest vegetation. Once out of the gully, the track leads through open forest of narrow leaf peppermint trees. A base level walking track that winds through state forest, which traverses Deep Gully with its temperate rainforest vegetation. Once through the gully, the track leads through an open forest of narrow leaf peppermint trees. Keep an eye out for relics of a strong mining history.
properties.a: Access to the walking track is directly from the Mitta Mitta Historic Reserve (Mitta Mitta township) with many camping options in and around the Mitta Mitta area.

g: Walk · 6.5 km return · 3 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Limited signage
properties.d: Freestone Creek Walking Track takes off from the Blue Pool Day Visitor Area carpark and follows the Freestone Creek North. The track pops up on Freestone Creek Road for a section until just after Gladstone Creek Bridge where it takes a contouring route above the road until coming back down above Mckinnons Point. The route then follows Mckinnons Point 4WD track across the Freestone Creek for a short distance before ducking off the road and continuing up a moist gully. This pleasant section provides quite a bit more shade and a different array of plant species to the other sections of the walk. As the track begins to climb and head back South you are rewarded with stunning views of the……
properties.a: From Briagolong, head north along the Freestone Creek Road for approximately 10km (10 minutes) until you reach Blue Pool. Limited parking is available at the Blue Pool Day Visitor Area, with overflow parking available at the Blue Pool Campground. The loop commences from the Day Visitor Area and finishes where the Fern Gully Loop takes off on the West side of Blue Pool.

g: Walk · 1 km return · 30 min · Grade 4
properties.t: Rough many obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: A short walk to a historic batery relic from the gold mining days. The walk departs from the Deptford camping area on the eastern side of the Nicholson River.
properties.a: Access is on the eastern side of the Nicholson River at Deptford.

g: Horse riding · 16 km return · 4+ hrs · Moderate
properties.d: This is a 16km ride starting out of Andersons Mill which is about 4km from the main Marysville Rd. Andersons Mill has plenty of room for vehicles and floats but will often have other campers there as well. The campsite has 12 horse yards and room for more electric yards. It also has a water trough fed by a spring. The site has toilets and fire pits along with a couple of picnic tables. The ride leaves Andersons Mill and travels via Andersons Mill Road and then via Rons Track and Paradise Plains Road and Keppel Lookout Road to Keppels Lookout. There is plenty of room to tie up horses on the edge of the carpark and a short walk leads to the lookout which offers stunning views over the…
properties.a: From Marysville take Lyell Street to the south which runs into Paradise Plains road. Head past the Marysville reservoir before reaching Anderson Mill road. Here turn right and continue on for approximately 4km. The Anderson Mill campground is on your left hand side and clearly sign posted. Unload your horse at Anderson Mill to commence your ride.

g: Walk · 1.8 km return · 40 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occassional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Starting at Rocky Ned day visitor area, this short walk crosses over and then follows Rocky Ned Creek for views of Rocky Ned Falls. Along the way take your time to explore the granite boulder formations and take in the views looking north across the Lima East valley.
properties.a: You can access the Rocky Ned Falls Walk from the day visitor area and campground. Turn off the Midland Highway onto Lima East Road at Swanpool. Rocky Ned Campground and Day Visitor site is then located about 20 kilometres on the right hand side. 2wd dirt road access.

properties.n: Aberfeldy Backroad Tour - Woods Point to Jamieson - Gooleys Creek
g: 4WD · 5.4 km return · 1–4 hrs · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. Heading southeast out of Woods Point down Coster Street, this side trip takes you to the site of Gooleys Creek, once a significant gold mining settlement for the ‘Never Mind’ and ‘Franklin’ gold mines, named after William Gooley, who discovered gold in the creek in 1861. You will also pass by the route cut by McMillans party, to link the gold mining settlements from Omeo to Woods Point and the Jordan. If seeking a campsite, the side trip passes near the Comet Flat Reserve. Looks for the turn-off down Noble Spur Track about 1.2km out of Woods Point.
properties.a: This side trip is accessed off the main street of Woods Point, heading east on Coster Street, opposite the Woods Point Hotel.

g: Walk · 1.5 km one way · under 1 hr · Grade 2.1
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.a: Reed walking track links Limestone Box forest walk with Gippsland Lakes Discovery Trail. Starts halfway down Limestone Box forest walk, crosses Armstrong Road and continues generally downhill to the Gippsland Lakes Discovery Trail 100 m up from Scriveners Road.

g: Walk · 2.5 km return · under 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Gentle hills · No steps · Limited signage
properties.d: This walk meanders towards the Aberfeldy river from Donnelly’s Creek Rd, take in views of recovering forest and historic artefacts in the area. At the boiler you can return via the same route or take a slightly steeper return loop by crossing the bridge and following the trail up the southern slope. Toombon was a booming gold mining township in the late 1800s, featuring a population of around 700, a hotel, post office, church and school at its peak. Also present is the 300m deep Toombon Mine, considered to be the most successful in the area. Today, many reminders tell the story of the area's history.
properties.a: The trail head is found along Donelly’s Creek Rd, accessible from Walhalla Rd directly from the North or via Sullivan’s or Merrington's Trk to the South. Please drive considerately as there is limited parking and walkers using the area.

g: Walk · 11.6 km one way · 3 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This spectacular 12km walk starts at the Suspension Bridge and follows the Murrindindi River the entire length of the Reserve before concluding at the Cascades. The trail crosses over five footbridges and offers river views through a variety of forest types from tall open forest to damp ferny gullies. This walk is accessible from most of the Murrindindi picnic and camping sites.
properties.a: From Melbourne, travel along the Melba Highway to the intersection of Murrindindi Road just before Devlins Bridge. Turn right and drive on for 10km to the Reserve. The Suspension Bridge picnic area is at the Rangers Station and the start of the Murrindindi Walk is at the metal Suspension Bridge over the Murrindindi River. Alternatively continue 9km along Murrindindi Road to the Cascades picnic area and cross the road to the Cascades Walk to access the Murrindindi Walk over the Cascade bridges.

g: Mountain bike · 5.2 km one way · under 1 hr · Difficult
properties.d: This is a descending cross-country track with a few berms, and earth and log jumps. The track travels through open forest and finishes at the carpark trailhead. A cross-country descending trail at Nowa Nowa MTB Park.
properties.a: Nowa Nowa MTB Park is located on the Nowa Nowa - Buchan Rd, approx. 1.5 km from Nowa Nowa township.

g: Walk · 2.9 km return · 1 hr · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Well formed track · Gentle hills · Limited signage
properties.d: The North Red Gums Walk is a largely flat open walk which provides a good idea of the vegetation which once covered the landscape in this district. Larger specimens of E. tereticornis can be found at the Northern end of the walk near the Recreation Reserve.
properties.a: The Briagolong Red Gum Reserve is located just South of the township of Briagolong on the East side of the Briagolong Road. A picnic area with information shelter is located on the North side of O’Connor Road which cuts through the centre of the reserve.

g: Mountain bike · 1.5 km return · under 1 hr · Easy with Intermediate Sections
Walk · 1.5 km return · under 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Gentle hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: A walking track in typical lowland forest between the East Gippsland Rail Trail and the Princes Hwy. This track is part of a greater loop encompassing the Nowa Nowa Arm foreshore and Lake Tyers State Park.
properties.a: The track can be accessed from the Rail Trail heading west out of the Nowa Nowa township, or alternatively from Old Colquhoun Road.

g: Mountain bike · 3.4 km one way · under 1 hr · Intermediate
properties.a: From the Shuttle drop off point, take the track across the road and shortly after, bear left onto the link track to the gravity trails. This link track takes you to the start of Tip Top Run

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Timbarra Loop - Mt Stewart Track
g: 4WD · 3 km return · 1–4 hrs · Difficult (Black Diamond)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with reasonable 4WD experience or 4WD training. This side trip heads up a granite hill to the peak of Mt Stewart, overlooking the clearing at Glenmore in the Buchan River Valley. The 340 hectare Mount Stewart Natural Features and Scenic Reserve carries heathlands growing on shallow rocky soil and includes waterfalls on the Mellick Munjie Creek. The Buchan Valley is home to the Krauatungalung clan of the Gunaikurnai people and holds great culture significance as a traditional meetings place during seasonal migrations.
properties.a: At the Glenmore Road/Mt Stewart Track intersection, head up Mt Stewart Track for 1.5km to Mt Stewart summit.

g: Mountain bike · 1.6 km one way · Difficult
properties.d: This trail starts with a long climb (Cathedral Climb) to the lookout, utilising numerous climbing switchbacks. It then heads down the hill (Buxton BOM) and the real fun begins with tight berms and lots of jumps. BEWARE of the gap jumps and don’t let your ambition get confused with your ability. Keep your speed in check. This trail rejoins Acheron Ridge just before the carpark.

g: Walk · 12 km return · 1–4 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · No steps · No directional signage
properties.d: This 12km walk will take you on an old tramway through the towering mountain ash forest. The trail will take you to the West Tanjil River and the Tramway Falls rapids. The return walk may take 2-4 hours and dogs are allowed on the trail. The trail may be subject to snow cover over the winter months. This walk follows the old tramway lines through Antarctic Beech and Mountain Ash forest, meandering down to the West Tanjil River and Tramway Falls rapids.
properties.a: Access via Saxtons Rd Tanjil Bren, just off the Mt Baw Baw Tourist Rd.

g: Mountain bike · 0.15 km one way · under 1 hr · Easy
properties.d: This easy 150m track will connect you to Tip Top Run.
properties.a: From the shuttle drop off point, take the track across the road and shortly after, bear left. You are now on the link track which connects you to Tip Tp Run.

g: Mountain bike · 13.3 km return · 1–4 hrs · Intermediate
properties.d: This is the longest trail in the Buxton betwork, starting at the car park, and is filled with jumps, berms, log drops and loads of exhilarating fast singletrack. It includes the famous spider gully, which starts with a series of tight corners weaving through tall tree ferns before opening out and increasing in speed as it descends. This trail finishes back at the car park.

g: Horse riding · 3 km return · under 1 hr · Basic
Walk · 6 km return · 1.5 hrs · Grade 2.1
properties.t: Well formed track · Flat · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This early 1900s railway line was built to carry timber from mills in the surrounding forest. Of the seven original bridges, only the Noojee trestle bridge remains. At 102m long and 21m high it is the tallest wooden trestle bridge in Victoria. The walk takes you to the top of the bridge providing elevated views of the tall forest as you walk across the historic wooden bridge high above the gully. A must do for those who enjoy the thrill of being up high! This short ride begins at the eastern end of Noojee, at the Noojee Trestle Bridge Rail Trail trailhead where there is parking and public toilets. The trail follows the alignment of the early 1900s railway line which was built to carry…
properties.a: Access via School Rd in Noojee to begin at the eastern end or via the Trestle Bridge off the Mt Baw Baw Tourist Rd to the West of Noojee.

g: Walk · 3 km return · 2 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Very steep · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: A 3 km stunning walk amongst the low snow gums with views across the surrounding alpine valleys, leading up to the historical Craigs hut. It is a well formed track with some short steep sections. A good way to visit Craigs Hut if you want to stretch your legs or for those in 2WD vehicles.
properties.a: From Mansfield follow the Mt. Buller Rd to Mirimbah. Turn left onto Mt. Stirling Rd and follow to Telephone Box Junction (T.B.J). From here, The Circuit Road can be driven in either direction. Follow Circuit Road 17kms from T.B.J in a clockwise direction, or 29kms in an anti-clockwise direction. The drive is normally accessible to all vehicles, but can have rough sections. The Circuit Road is seasonally closed at T.B.J from the Friday before the Queen's Birthday weekend until the Thursday before the Melbourne Cup Weekend.

g: Walk · 4.6 km one way · 2 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Limited signage
properties.d: Mt Hedrick Walking Track is a scenic walk which predominantly follows a ridgeline from Mt Hedrick to Huggetts Lookout. Stunning views are available to the North with unique rocky outcrops and boulders providing an insight into the geology of the Avon - Mt Hedrick Natural Features and Scenic Reserve. Caution should be taken in these sections especially in wet conditions. It is also recommended that those completing a return walk would follow the same route along the ridgeline from Huggetts Lookout to Mt Hedrick carpark. A grade 4 walking track that climbs Mount Hedrick and crosses to the Huggetts lookout.
properties.a: From the township of Heyfield take Weir Rd North for 10km and turn Right onto Lanigan Rd. Turn Left off Lanigan Rd onto Millers Rd and follow for 7.5km. At Bulldog Junction turn right and continue on Huggetts Rd until you reach the Mt Hedrick Picnic Area. The Walking track begins on the East side of the road. The opposite end of the track can be accessed from Newry via Three Chain Rd and then Kentucky Rd. Turn left onto Huggett’s Track and after around 1.5km the walking track takes off from the left from Huggett's Lookout.

g: Mountain bike · 4.8 km one way · under 1 hr · Intermediate
properties.d: This track starts a bit higher than the other tracks and makes a fast descent crossing track 3 and ending at the carpark trailhead.
properties.a: Nowa Nowa MTB Park is located on the Nowa Nowa - Buchan Rd, approx. 1.5 km from Nowa Nowa township.

g: Trail bike · 101 km one way · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: Mostly a medium grade of difficulty with a few more difficult sections, this is a one-way route to the township of Dargo, where fuel, accommodation, food and some motorcycle spares and repairs are available. The route comprises open forest roads and narrow steep and hilly tracks. There are some serious steep sections that may become slippery following rain. There are some creek and river crossings which are usually shallow.
properties.a: To access the Mount Taylor Trail Bike Visitor Area from Bairnsdale, follow the signs to Wy Yung, and then travel north along the Bullumwaal Road for approximately 7km. Turn right onto Boyds Road, follow Boyds Rd. across Mt Taylor Creek and up past a quarry on the left. The trail Bike visitor area is 400m past the quarry. It is immediately past the intersection of Howitt Spur Rd and Jones Rd.

g: 4WD · 55 km one way · 8 hrs · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with some 4WD experience or training. This route takes you into the Thomson Water Supply Catchment, explores the history of the Jordan Valley Goldfields and its early settlements and cemeteries. In Aberfeldy township, there is an optional side trip to Hanging Rock (4WD Grade – Very Difficult). If not doing this side trip, head north out of Aberfeldy on the Walhalla Road for about 2km to reach O’Keefe Track on your right. Here you can choose to do the optional side trip to Aberfeldy Crossing (4WD Grade – Difficult) or continue along Walhalla Road for a further 10.5km, where you can then turn left to do an optional side trip down Victor Spur Track (4WD Grade – Medium) or…
properties.a: Commences from the historic township of Aberfeldy, heading north on the Walhalla Road. Note – This route is subject to seasonal road closures from 1 May to the end of November each year.

properties.n: Aberfeldy Backroad Tour - Woods Point to Jamieson
g: 4WD · 55 km one way · 4+ hrs · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. This route from Woods Point to Jamieson, with optional side trips, is dotted with the relics of settlements and mines built post the discovery of gold at Enochs Point in 1857. Settlements were quickly established at Gaffneys Creek, Woods Point, Kevington and Ten Mile. Woods Point was once a thriving township boasting 36 hotels, stores, business offices, police station, churches, medical centres, banks, post office and factories. The decrease in mining saw the population plummet from around 2000 to one or two hundred in the 1890s. The 1939 Black Friday fires destroyed the township, killing one person at each of…
properties.a: Commences from Woods Point heading northeast along the Mansfield-Woods Point Road.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Omeo to Dargo
g: 4WD · 80 km one way · 1–4 hrs · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. Can be slippery when wet and subject to snow. This tour links the rural towns of Omeo and Dargo via Mt Birregun, with breathtaking views of the surrounding landscapes. It is an easy drive over the summer months, but the roads can get quite wet over winter and be subject to snow. The tour starts at Omeo’s Livingstone Creek Park, which is the base for the Omeo MTB trails, with picnic and overnight camping facilities. From Livingstone Creek Park follow Creek Street into Omeo, turn right onto the Great Alpine Road, and then left onto Cassilis Road. Take another right onto Upper Livingstone Road, and then follow…
properties.a: The tour starts at Omeo’s Livingstone Creek Park, heading southwest out of Omeo on the Great Alpine Road.

g: Mountain bike · 0.2 km one way · under 1 hr · Easy
Walk · 0.2 km one way · 9 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Well formed track · Short steep hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: A short link walk through private property joining the Michaeldene trail and the Tree Fern Gully Trail. The trailhead can be found at the back of the Marysville recreation ground and over one of the steel bridges straddling the Steavenson River. This dual purpose track links Tree Fern Gully Trail and Michaeldene Trail. Providing a link between two trails, this multi purpose trail is situated in the township of Marysville.
properties.a: From Marysville Information Centre take the Tree Fern Gully Trail for about 500m and head behind the recreation oval. Here there is a metal bridge over the Steavenson River take the trail to the North East where it links up with the Michaeldene Trail near Lady Talbot Drive.

g: Walk · 95 km one way · multi-day · Grade 4
properties.t: Rough many obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · No directional signage
properties.d: The Upper Yarra Walking Track is the oldest long distance walking track in Australia and it provides a challenging walk along old logging tramlines and old vehicle tracks finishing at Mt Whitelaw on the Alpine Walking Track. Passing through tall eucalypt forest and fern gullies, this grade 4 multi day walking track is suited to the experienced bushwalker. To extend the walk and follow the original route of the track, add on the Walk Into History Track starting at Warburton and finishing at the Ada Tree Picnic Area. The Original walk also included the section of the Alpine Walking Track from Mount Whitelaw to Walhalla. The Upper Yarra Walking track was the first long distance recreational…
properties.a: The official start of the Upper Yarra walking track is at the Ada Tree Picnic Area. From Powelltown, head east along the Yarra Junction-Noojee Rd (C425) for 6km then turn left up Big Creek Road. Travel along Big Creek Road for 22km and turn right down Federal Road. Travel along Federal Road for 3km until you reach the Ada Tree Picnic Area.The track ends on the Alpine Walking Track, so the closest pickup point would be to continue the Alpine Walking Track to the north and finish on Thomson Valley road, or to the south, finishing at the Mt Baw Baw village.

g: Walk · 34 km one way · 48 hrs · Grade 5
properties.t: Rough unformed · Very steep and difficult · Occasional steps · No directional signage
properties.d: The walking track, as well as being interesting historically, traverses some very scenic forest with camp and picnic sites along the way. The total network of tracks that make up Track 96 total 60kms of walking, providing various degrees of difficulty for the casual or experienced walker. The first section may be commenced just north of the Blue Pools walking tracks. Track 96 was retraced and cleared during the 1990s thanks mainly to the efforts of the Ben Cruachan Walking Club who have helped retain a vital link with our past..On leaving the town of Gladstone, Track 96 crossed what is now private property known as Paddy Melon Gully. To pick up Track 96 you will have to walk around the……
properties.a: From the intersection with Beverley’s Rd travel 24.5km or 25 minutes North on the Dargo Road (C601) to the Pretty Boy Hill carpark. To access the Blue Pool carpark from Briagolong follow the Freestone Creek Road approximately 10km or 10 minutes. Campsites along the route can be accessed via the Freestone Creek Road.

g: Walk · 3 km return · 1 hr · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Well formed track · Flat · Limited signage
properties.d: The South block displays similar vegetation to the North block with some slightly more open areas. It is reasonably flat and can easily be added onto the North loop if you wish to extend your walk.
properties.a: The Briagolong Red Gum Reserve is located just South of the township of Briagolong on the East side of the Briagolong Road. A picnic area with information shelter is located on the North side of O’Connor Road which cuts through the centre of the reserve.

properties.n: Aberfeldy Backroad Tour - Woods Point to Jamieson - Star of the West
g: 4WD · 3.6 km return · 1–4 hrs · Difficult (Black Diamond)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with reasonable 4WD experience or 4WD training. This side trip to the Old Star of the West Goldmine is well worth the effort. The steep 4WD track can be walked if not suitable to drive. This goldmine was the richest of the local gold mines producing 33,000 ounces of gold (worth $90 million in 2024 values). Evidence remains of mullock heaps, audits, furnace sites and huts. At the end of the vehicle track you can further explore the site via the short Star of the West Goldmine Walk.
properties.a: This side trip is accessed off the Mansfield – Woods Point Road near Kevington and heads down Star of West Track.

g: Mountain bike · 4.5 km one way · under 1 hr · Intermediate
properties.d: A fast tight flow trail which starts 100 metres below Tower Road from the shuttle turnaround point. A variety of riders will enjoy this track if you have the required skill and stamina to master it. The trail encompasses many jumps, dips, berms, rock gully crossings and some rock slabs. It drops quickly down through tall open eucalypt forest and offers easy but technical features along the way, ending at the picnic area.
properties.a: From Bairnsdale, travel north through Wy Yung and follow the Bullumwaal Rd. The intersection to Mount Taylor is where the bitumen road turns to gravel.

g: Walk · 1.5 km return · 1.25 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This track connects the Mitta Mitta Historic Reserve and The Mill camp site. It is a pleasant walk through streamside vegetation with constant views of the powerful Mitta Mitta river.
properties.a: Access directly from the Mitta Mitta township either via the Mitta Mitta Historic Reserve of the Mill camp site.

g: Mountain bike · 1 km one way · under 1 hr · Very Easy
Walk · 1 km one way · 18 min · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Well formed trk · Flat · Occassional steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: Kendalls Link Trail is a short 1.1 km walk that connects Kendalls Camp to the Boys Camp. This flat, well formed track is a great short stroll through the riparian bush. Easy ride from Kendalls to The Boys camping ground.

g: Walk · 6 km return · 1–4 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: A 6km challenging circuit through local forest, with some steep sections including a steep descent into a gully before climbing onto the ridge. The track passes the old plane crash site and the Explosive Magazine site.
properties.a: Access is via the Great Alpine Rd approx 2km from Bruthen township.

g: Walk · 1.2 km one way · 30 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: The return walk to the lookout begins at the J.A. Jones Memorial Reserve on the eastern edge of town adjacent to the Murray toMountains Rail Trail. Nearby, Paul’s Gold Battery stands adjacent to several gold mining adits (tunnels) into Reform Hill. Ascendthe Reform Hill Monument Track to the T-intersection then turn left to visit the Hume & Hovell Memorial. From here it is possible to take two different routes tothe lookout, both approximately equal in distance. A large loop can be formed by combining all three tracks. The Reform Hill lookout provides visitors with views ofthe Ovens Valley, Mount Buffalo and the Victorian Alps. Crops of hops, vineyards and pasture give the valley its…
properties.a: The site can be accessed via the Reform Hill walking track network. The best starting point is Jones Reserve located on the Great Alpine Road in Myrtleford between the Hardware store and Rays Ski Shop.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Omeo to Buchan
g: 4WD · 167 km one way · 4+ hrs · Easy (Green Circle)
properties.d: This drive is suitable for novice drivers in all-wheel drive and high range 4WDs. This half to full day tour (depending on stops) heads from Omeo across the Limestone Road to Gelantipy before descending down into Buchan. This road can be closed due to snow over the winter months but showcases some fabulous areas of the Alpine National Park. This is a great way to cut across from the Omeo Valley to the Buchan Valley and taking in some new sites along the way. The tour begins at Omeo’s Livingstone Creek Park. Follow Creek Street, then turn left onto Great Alpine Road, veering left onto Omeo Highway. Next, turn right onto Benambra Road and take another left towards McMillan's Lookout, for…
properties.a: The tour starts at Omeo’s Livingstone Creek Park, heading north on Day Avenue and onto the Omeo Highway. The route is subject to roaming stock and feral horses are widespread and are often seen on the roads so drive with care. Roads subject to frost, ice and snow which may lead to temporary road closures – Chains should be carried during winter.

g: Mountain bike · 8.5 km return · under 1 hr · Easy
Horse riding · 8.5 km return · 1–4 hrs · Moderate
Walk · 8.5 km return · 1.5 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: An enjoyable walk through forests and past farmland with the option of lunch in Marysville at the halfway point. You may see other users on this shared trail as mountain bikes and horse riders occasionally also use this trail. A well-defined trail shared with walkers and horse riders. A mostly contoured trail but with some ups and downs which makes for an enjoyable ride to exercise the heart and mind. This circuit ride starts and ends at Andersons Mill which is about 4km south of Marysville. Andersons Mill has plenty of room for vehicles and floats but will often have other campers there as well. The campsite has 12 horse yards and room for more electric yards. It also has a water trough…
properties.a: The trail starts from Anderson Mill campground. To get to Anderson Mill from Marysville,head up Lyell street off the main street. Lyell Street becomes Paradise Plains Road. Continue on Paradise Plains Road, past the Marysville reservoir, and shortly after, turn right down Anderson Mill Road. Continue on for approximately 2.5km. The turnoff to Anderson Mill campground is on your left hand side and clearly sign posted

g: Mountain bike · 4.9 km one way · 1–4 hrs · Intermediate
properties.d: Main climb trail at Nowa Nowa. This trail is rated as intermediate. This track is the designated climbing track for the mountain bike park. The track gently winds up to the start point for the 4 descending tracks.
properties.a: Nowa Nowa MTB Park is located on the Nowa Nowa - Buchan Rd, approx. 1.5 km from Nowa Nowa township.

g: Walk · 0.15 km return · under 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occassional steps · Limited signage
properties.d: Explore relics of the old Red Jacket ghost town. This track climbs up to the site of an old boiler and various other old relics left over from the towns mining past.

properties.n: Aberfeldy Backroad Tour - Jordan Valley - Hanging Rock
g: 4WD · 9.2 km return · 20 min · Very Difficult (Double Black Diamond)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with extensive 4WD experience and advanced training. Located on the banks of the Aberfeldy River, Hanging Rock was a popular picnic spot in the late 1800s to early 1900s. Head east out of Aberfeldy township down Cullens Track. After 2km, veer right onto Comet Spur Track, which is a steeply rutted (traverse in dry weather only). Travel 1.8km before turning left onto Eaton Track. A further 800m along, you will find the start of the Hanging Rock Walking Track (1.2km return).
properties.a: In the Aberfeldy township take Cullens Track, opposite the telephone box.

g: Walk · 0.3 km return · 5 min · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Formed track · Flat · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This short historic walk of about 100 metres is suitable for young families, although parents need to be mindful of the steep escarpment beyond the barriers. The area is recovering from being burnt in the Beechworth-Library Road bushfire of 2009. This short walk through mixed species eucalypt forest leads to a lookout over an old mining area, with a steam boiler associated with eucalypt oil extraction of later years to be seen. You return along the same track.
properties.a: From Beechworth head approx. 7 km south along the Buckland Gap Rd (towards Myrtleford/Gapsted) until you reach the Buckland Gap. Head East onto Lady Newton Drive for 250m then onto Jensens Tk. Bates Dam is well sign posted once on Lady Newton Drive.

g: Walk · 0.3 km return · 9 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Well formed trk · Short steep hills · Many steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Situated at the foothills of the Rubicon State Forest, Snobs Banyarmbite Falls offers spectacular views as the pristine water fed by the Snobs Creek flows over the 100m drop of rocky outcrops. Take the winding stepped path descending under the large Blanket Leaf trees down to the two viewing platforms which offer wonderful opportunities to take photos of the impressive, tiered waterfall rushing and tumbling down over the large boulders.
properties.a: From nearby Thornton, follow the Goulburn Valley Highway B 340 to the Snobs Creek pub, 5km before Eildon. Turn right on to Snobs Creek road and drive south for 5.7 km.

g: Walk · 8 km return · 5.5 hrs · Grade 5
properties.t: Rough unformed · Very steep · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: A challenging walk through dry eucalypt forest littered with examples of historic mining works. This hike follows a spur line, which offers spectacular views of the Mitta valley and surrounding mountains. During spring, a more colourful walk can be enjoyed with wild flowers often in bloom. Note that this walk contains steep terrain, good navigation skills and level of fitness are required.
properties.a: Access via Upper Pioneer trail to walk from the bottom of the trail to the top. Access to the top of Mt Welcome Hike, head approximately 3.4 kms along the Omeo Highway towards Omeo from Mitta Mitta township. Then turn right onto Mt Disappointment Track and travel approximately 4kms to the start of Mt Welcome Hike. 4WD all weather access only.

g: Walk · 10 km return · 4 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Flowing from the Monda road green break down the mountain this track winds under some large Mountain Ash and 1939 regeneration forest into fern gullies over numerous timber bridges. Eventually you can head into the Wirrawilla Rainforest Walk and up the old Quarry road track back to Monda carpark. Alternatively you can commence at Wirrawilla and for those that like a more invigorating walk you might like to consider joining up with the Myrtle Gully Circuit for the whole 17km Tanglefoot trail experience.
properties.a: One option is to head to Healesville then take Myers Creek Road for 12 km to Monda road. Turn right at Monda road and wind your way up 5km, past Mt St Lenard, to the Tanglefoot Carpark. The walking track trailhead is on the opposite side of the Monda road. Alternatively, from Healesville, take the Myers Creek road for nearly 13km. Take a right at Sylvia Creek Road and follow this for about 4.5km until you see the sign for Wirrawilla carpark. The trail can be accessed from this site.

g: Mountain bike · 3 km one way · under 1 hr · Difficult
properties.d: Mt Taylor Flow Track is rated black diamond and starts at the top trailhead/ shuttle turnaround point. It is well sign posted and ends 3km later at the bottom trailhead/picnic area. The track consists of many tight bermed corners, gap jumps, kickers, "a" and "b" lines and rocky sections. It crosses Goodes Track (a road) and Milky Way XC Tk.
properties.a: Follow the Bullumwaal Rd north from Bairnsdale, passing Wy Yung and Mt Taylor Fire Station and further along past the Mt Taylor hall. 18km from Bairnsdale, at the end of the bitumen road, turn left into the Mt Taylor Mountain bike park. The trailhead is 300 metres up the picnic area.

g: Walk · 0.7 km one way · under 1 hr
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · Occassional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This track links the James Reserve campground to the Lima East Day Visitor Area and also provides access onto the Lima East Boulders Walk.
properties.a: You can access this walking track from either the James Reserve campground or the Lima East Day Visitor Area.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Omeo to Buchan - Rams Horn Track
g: 4WD · 7.6 km return · 1–4 hrs · Very Difficult (Double Black Diamond)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with extensive 4WD experience and advanced training. This seasonal side trip takes you to Rams Horn. It travels the rocky Rams Horn Track to Rams Horn carpark. From there it is a short 10 minute walk to Rams Horn, one of the largest isolated outcrops of the Snowy River Volcanics in the Cobberas area. Its southern face rises vertically about 50 metres.
properties.a: This side track starts about 50km east of Benambra on the Limestone Road, at the intersection of Limestone Road and Rams Horn Track.

g: Walk · 1.5 km return · under 1 hr · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Formed track · Flat · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: A beautiful walk through the wet montane forest, you will surround yourself with tall tree ferns and if you're quiet enough may hear or spot a lyrebird running about. The walk ends with a stunning view of the waterfall.
properties.a: From Mansfield take the Mansfield Mount Buller road towards Mount Buller before turning left onto onto Carters road and then follow the signs for waterfall walk.

g: Mountain bike · 0.16 km return · under 1 hr · Easy
Walk · 1.7 km return · 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Gentle hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Starting on the boundary of pine plantation and the state forest. Along this track you will see beautiful native flora and fauna, spectacular views and naturally occuring waterfalls.
properties.a: From Benalla take the Midland Highway towards Swanpool for 16.8KM, turn right onto Lima Road for 20.6KM. Turn left onto Police Track and follow for 4.1KM, then turn left onto the E6 Track and follow for 900M. Take the 3rd left and follow the road until you reach the Rocky Ned Carpark. Please note this is Four Wheel Drive Access only.

g: Mountain bike · 2.3 km one way · under 1 hr · Extreme
properties.d: This advanced level downhill MTB track is a double black diamond due to its fast-paced technical nature. It starts below the communication tower off Tower Road and rapidly descends 300 metres through natural bushland with fast corners and big jumps. It crosses large rock slabs, optional earth jumps and the infamous ‘Cabbage Patch’ before several jumps and ending with a jump beside a dam into the picnic area.
properties.a: From Bairnsdale, travel north through Wy Yung and follow the Bullumwaal Rd. The intersection to Mount Taylor is where the bitumen road turns to gravel.

g: Walk · 3.9 km return · 1.5 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · Occassional steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: This walk passes through beautiful Mountain Ash forests and down into cool temperate rainforest, with highlights that include crossing an impressive timber trestle bridge, a look inside a small heritage-listed sawmill and walking along the aqueduct that feeds the Royston Power Station. The Rubicon Valley Historic Area has been set aside for the protection of the area’s historic sites and values. Timber harvesting used to be the major industry of the region, beginning in the early 1900s. There were eight sawmills operating in the forest in the first half of the century. Note: The walk passes alongside an aqueduct, so care should be taken, particularly with children, not to fall into this…
properties.a: From Melbourne, follow the Maroondah Highway; turn right onto the Taggerty-Thornton Road and right again onto Rubicon Road. Once you drive past the bridge over the Rubicon River, the road name changes to Royston Road. Continue along Royston Road for a further 5.7km to the carpark at the start of the walk. Note - this carpark is the starting point for of the Rubicon Dam Walk also.

g: Walk · 4.2 km return · under 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: The track gets its name from the series of bends constructed along an old logging tramline established by William Richards that allowed for timber to be hauled from the forest along a steady descent from Mississippi Fireline towards Big Pats Creek. The walk starts in the Big Pats Recreation and Camping area. Begin at the stairs and make your way up 'The Curves' to Mississippi Fireline and return via the same route down the steady decent back into Big Pats Creek Recreation Area. Alternatively you can continue along the remainder of 9km of the Richards Tramline to Brahams Rd. (Please see 'Richards Tramline' for more information).
properties.a: From Melbourne head out along the Maroondah Highway to Lilydale. Past Lilydale, head right onto Warburton Highway. Continue the extent of Warburton Highway, through the township of Warburton onto Woods Point Road. Just after you cross the Yarra River about 3km up Wood Point Road take a right turn up Riverside Drive and take your next left up Big Pats Creek Road. Continue along this road through the small settlement of Big Pats Creek until you cross the creek itself, then take you first right just after the bridge up Burns Road. Not far up this road you will reach the Big Pats Recreation Area…

g: Mountain bike · 0.25 km return · under 1 hr · Easy
properties.d: Loop ride suitable for beginners

g: Mountain bike · 25 km one way · 4+ hrs · Intermediate
Walk · 25 km one way · 48 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Well formed track · Short steep hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Although predominately ridden by bike, this trail with its gentle grades, beautiful forests and interesting history is also a great walk. The times and distance for this trail assume starting point is where the Gippsland Lakes Discovery Trail joins the East Gippsland Rail Trail. If starting the walk at Bruthen, add 11km. You can link this ride in with the East Gippsland Rail Trail to ride from Bairnsdale to Lakes Entrance (65km, full day one-way or leisurely two day ride with an overnight break in Bruthen), or from Bruthen to Lakes Entrance (36km) or from Forestech to Lakes Entrance (13km). The track undulates through stringybark forest then joins the old Mississippi Tramway alignment…
properties.a: The start of the track is near the intersection of Seaton Track and the East Gippsland Rail Trail, approx. 12km east of Bruthen township. This location is also accessible by car, via Bruce Rd and Seaton Tk.

g: Walk · 2.1 km one way · 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Many steps · Limited signage
properties.d: From the Channel lookout, follow the stairs down to the Avon river. This 2.1km grade 3 walk follows the Avon river through the spectacular channel gorge. The track is part of the extended Avon walking track. The Channel is the centrepiece of the Avon reserve; amagnificent gorge created by the Avon River carving itsway through the silt and sandstone over millennia. Thesteep sides of the gorge are covered in native vegetation,with shady Casuarinas in abundance. Crags punctuate theriverbed, creating a system of pools and rapids thatprovide important habitat for aquatic life.
properties.a: From Maffra take the Maffra-Briagolong Road out of Maffra towards Boisdale. Continue through Boisdale towards Valencia Creek. Turn Left onto Luckman's Road (3km beyond Boisdale) and finally right into Warrigal-Toms Creek Road. From here turn left onto Green Hills Road and then right onto Channel Track. Please note, the nearby Channel Road does not access the Channels carpark.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Dargo to Swifts Creek
g: 4WD · 77 km one way · 4+ hrs · Medium (Blue Square)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with some 4WD experience or training. This route is celebrated for its popular campsites and stunning views along Upper Dargo Road, where you can enjoy the scenic beauty of both the Dargo and Wentworth Rivers throughout the day. Able to be completed in a half day, you may choose to extend your trip by overnighting in one or more of the campgrounds along this route. Start your journey in Dargo, an area first mapped in the 1850s. Head north along Dargo Plains Rd and turn right onto Upper Dargo Rd. Here, you’ll find a number of camping options, including Two-Mile Flat, Italian Flat, Jimmy Iverson’s, and Ollie’s Jump Up. Alternatively, you can camp by the large inside sweep…
properties.a: The tour commences from Dargo, heading north along Dargo High Plains.

properties.n: High Country Backroad Tour - Mt Baldhead Loop - Nicholson River Track
g: 4WD · 37 km one way · 1–4 hrs · Difficult (Black Diamond)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with reasonable 4WD experience or 4WD training. This optional side trip cuts out the northern most section of the main Mt baldhead Loop, following alongside the upper Nicholson River, with its past history of mining and timber harvesting.
properties.a: This side trip commences from Marthavale and continues down Nicholson River Track.

g: Walk · 8 km one way · 2.5 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: An 8 km walk through open snow gum forest that circumnavigates the Dinner Plain village. The walk has a rough, rocky track surface with some short steep hills. The track is generally under snow in the winter months. The Montane walking track starts on the northern side of the Alpine hwy approximately 100m east of the main entrance to the Dinner Plains Village
properties.a: The walk starts at the Dinner Plain village and ends up on Dinner Plain Track approximately 3km south of the DP village. Dinner Plain Track has a seasonal road closure on it to vehicles between mid June and end October.

g: Mountain bike · 29 km one way · 1–4 hrs · Intermediate
properties.d: This intermediate trail through beautiful mountain forests starts at Lake Mountain and descends 1550m, with 500m of climbing, down into Marysville. It will take between 3 to 5 hours to complete, with lots of great views, steep berms, flowy descents and jumps with A and B line options. Bring plenty of snacks, water and spares because this is a strenuous remote country ride that requires your full attention.
properties.a: From Marysville, head towards Lake Mountain Alpine Resort on the Marysville-Woods Point Road. After 10km, turn right onto the Lake Mountain Road and continue for 10km to reach the Lake Mountain Resort. The trailhead is on the right as you enter the main carpark.

g: Scenic drive · 45 km return · 1–4 hrs · Easy
properties.d: Commencing from Marysville, Lady Talbot Drive is a scenic loop drive through the Taggerty River valley and beyond, passing through stands of Mountain Ash forests and ferns, with the ghostly white stags of dead Mountain Ash trees, killed in the 2009/10 bushfires in the distance. The drive offers numerous opportunities to stop during the first part of the drive, with short walks to Phantom Falls (800m, 30 mins return), Keppel Falls (2km, 1 hour return) and Taggerty Cascades (400m return to cascades or 1.2km return to Meeting of the Waters). The drive continues on up to Mt Margaret Gap and then loops back to Marysville. Do not undertake this drive during storm or high wind events due to…
properties.a: From Marysville head north to the roundabout and turn right down Marysville Woods Point road. Lady Talbot Drive starts here and continues for 46km along the Mt Margaret Road, through State Forest to the Buxton-Marysville Road and back to Marysville. Lady Talbot Drive is suitable for two wheel drive vehicles, but in dry weather only.

g: Mountain bike · 2 km one way · under 1 hr · Intermediate
Walk · 2 km return · 18 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Red Hill Trail stretches up the side of Red Hill to one of the town's green breaks where there is an excellent view of Sugarloaf. The track then descending down to meet the Michaeldene Trail in the nearby gully. Turn right to return to Marysville. A challenging shared use trail that heads up to the top of Red Hill from Marysville then down the other side joining with the Michaeldene trail. Turn right to return to Marysville. If you would like a longer ride, turn left to do the Michaeldene loop which returns back to Marysville. Holidaying in Marysville and looking to blow the cobwebs out? Walk or ride the Red Hill Trail to the north of the town and enjoy some great views over Marysville and…
properties.a: From the roundabout at the northern end of town, head towards Buxton along the Buxton-Marysville Road. After 200m you will see the start of the trail on your right.

g: Walk · 10 km return · 3 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Very steep · Many steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Boroondara Track can be accessed from Falls Creek road carpark 700m from the Murrindindi road junction. This circuit track encompasses both Wilhelmina Falls and a section of Murrindindi Walk. Stroll along the Boroondara Track to the Boroondara footbridge, before the track provides an invigorating walk upstream to the Wilhelmina Walk intersection. From here you can head down to the Wilhelmina Falls and take the time to enjoy the amazing views. Carefully descend down the rock trail to the Murrindindi River before turning to the left and following the river walk back to the Boroondara carpark.
properties.a: From Melbourne - travel along the Melba Highway to the intersection of Murrindindi Road just before Devlins Bridge. Turn right and drive 10km to the Reserve. Drive south along Murrindindi Road for approximately 6km to the junction of Falls road. Head left down Falls road for 700m until you see the Boroondara carpark on your left.

g: Walk · 0.25 km return · 10 min · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Well formed track · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: A short steep walk that takes you up to expansive views across the valley, including the small township of Woods Point.
properties.a: This walk is located at the small golf course in Woodspoint.

g: Horse riding · 12 km one way · 4+ hrs · Intermediate
Walk · 12 km one way · 4 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Rough many obstacles · Gentle hills · Occasional steps · Limited signage
properties.d: The Howqua River Walking Track is a popular walk, this walk will take you a total of 12.4 km through stunning native vegetation. You will follow the river flats for the majority of the walk and will give you the opportunity to cross over more than 30 river crossing. This walk gives you the ability to immerse yourself in the Victorian High Country and enjoy the stunning scenery. Spend time meandering through Australian native species as you take a long ride along the Howqua River, with opportunities to complete water crossing when water flow is high. Following the river flats you’ll cross over the river more than 30 times, this track becomes quite popular in the warmer months so care should…
properties.a: To Running Creek - from Mansfield follow the Woods Point Road toward Jamieson. At the Howqua Bridge turn left onto the Howqua River Road, follow for approx 6kms. Continue onto Steiners Rd for 2 kms and turn left into Running Creek.

properties.n: Aberfeldy Backroad Tour – Donnellys Creek Loop - Meringtons and Junction Hut
g: 4WD · 5.6 km one way · under 1 hr · Difficult (Black Diamond)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with reasonable 4WD experience or 4WD training. This side trip cuts out the northwestern section of the main Donnellys Creek Tour, rejoining the main route heading south. It takes you past Junction Hut and Meringtons Campgrounds and to the Aberfeldy River. You may choose to stay overnight at Junction Hut or at the more spacious Meringtons Campground. Junction Hut is set above the scenic junction of Donnellys Creek and the Aberfeldy River. 4WD vehicles may cross the river when conditions are suitable. At Meringtons, you can do Meringtons Walk that will take you to the Lone Grave of Charles Brown (Note – Access to the grave requires wading through the Aberfeldy River).…
properties.a: This side trip is accessed off Donnellys Creek Road and heads up Junction Track. Note – There is a deep river crossing at Junction, check depth prior to crossing.

g: Walk · 1.8 km return · 1 hr · Grade 4
properties.t: Rough many obstacles · Very steep · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: The walk is approximately 1.8km one way and provides access onto the Avon Walking Track with stunning views of the Avon River and surrounding hills. The walk is a steady downhill from Green Hill Rd to the Avon Walking track and so the walk back up to the road is more arduous. At least 2hrs should be allowed if completing a return walk. Nearby Green Hill Lookout provides a spot for a picnic with a view. A grade 4 walking track that provides alternative access to the Avon Walking Track.
properties.a: Green Hills Walking Track is located off Green Hills Rd via Kentucky Rd approximately 15 minutes from the township of Newry.

g: Walk · 1.8 km return · 30 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · No steps · Limited signage
properties.d: Follow what was once an old road (Middle Tyers Road) and walk underneath ancient Mountain Ash and Myrtle Beech. Enjoy glimpses of giant granite bolders along the walk and the diversity of plants, from the unique assemblage of flora to the mosses and fungi that cover the forest.
properties.a: To access the walk, follow Thomson Valley Rd north and turn onto the Mt Erica Rd. The walk starts approximately 1km before the Mt Erica carpark.

g: Mountain bike · 7.6 km return · 1–4 hrs · Easy with Intermediate Sections
Walk · 7.4 km return · 3 hrs · Grade 2.1
properties.t: Formed track · Gentle hills · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: This gently undulating shared trail links Marysville with Steavenson Falls Scenic Reserve and is the best way to approach the falls. Walkers and cyclists will pass through stands of tall Manna Gum, Mountain Ash and shady tree fern groves that surround the rushing Steavenson River. This trail is predominantly used by walkers so take it slow and cautious. The trail is wide and predominantly a gradual uphill to Steavenson Falls. so may not be suitable for smaller children. The trailhead is located just minutes from the center of town. This dual purpose trail provides an insight into the Marysville forest environment and continues on to join the popular tourist destination of Steavenson Falls.
properties.a: Head behind the Marysville Information Centre to the trailhead located at the furthest upstream bridge near the tennis courts in Gallipoli Park. The trail follows the Steavenson River with views over Marysville for 1.3km before crossing another bridge back to the southern bank. Keep left at the trail junction immediately after crossing the bridge and walk up to and across Yellow Dog road. The trail soon swings south, entering the narrowing rocky valley of the Steavenson Falls Scenic Reserve and finishes at Steavenson Falls Trail, with the falls to the left and the car park to the right.…

g: Mountain bike · 0.4 km one way · Intermediate
properties.d: This trail creates a short-cut removing all the climbing on Acheron Ridge and re-enters at the bottom of spider gully.

g: Walk · 8.6 km return · 3 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: You can begin the Myrtle Gully walk at either Tanglefoot picnic area or via Wirrawilla Rainforest. This 9km track follows the Myrtle Creek under some amazing Myrtle Beech trees before rising into the Mountain Ash stands then dipping in to the gullies at the Tanglefoot boardwalk. The walk can be experienced as a single loop or in conjunction with the Tanglefoot Loop as a 17km all day walk.
properties.a: Access via Wirrawilla Rainforest - From Healesville, head up the Myers Creek road for 13km. Take Sylvia Creek road to the right then continue on this well maintained forest road for 4.5km. On the hairpin bend you will find the start of the Wirrawilla carpark access road on your right. Alternately access via Tanglefoot Carpark - continue on Sylvia Creek road a further 3km to Tanglefoot carpark.

g: Walk · 0.6 km return · 27 min · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Well formed trk · Gentle hills · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: This short uphill walk takes you to a stand of Redwood trees that was part of an earlier planting trial into the suitability of Redwoods for timber production. See the Redwoods battle it out with the native eucalypts for survival.
properties.a: The Redwoods Walk is accessed from the Walindjerri picnic area. To get to the picnic area, head north past Narbethong for 2km along the Maroondah Highway, and then turn left onto Plantation Road. Continue along Plantation Road for 7.9km and then turn left onto Stoney Creek Road. Continue along Stoney Creek Road for 1.3km. You will pass an access road on your left hand side to the Walindjerri Camp. Continue on for another 200m to turn left into the day visitor site.

g: Mountain bike · 0.78 km one way · under 1 hr · Difficult
properties.d: Chicken Run is a hand built blue/black gravity trail which pretty much drops straight down from Tower Rd to join in with the Down Hill MTB track where it crosses Lookout Rd. It’s approx 800m long, steep and advanced unpredictable features.
properties.a: Chicken Run black/blue Downhill Mountainbike track starts directly off the side of Tower Road, approximately 100 m south of Lookout Rd (where the DH track starting ramp is).

properties.n: Link trail to Rocky Ned Falls Walk
g: Walk · 0.19 km one way · 3 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Short steep hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This link walking track provides access onto the Rocky Ned Falls walk and also down to Rocky Ned Creek Take the short 250 metre Rocky Ned Falls walk from the Rocky Ned 2 camp site.
properties.a: This link track is accessed from the Rocky Ned 2 campground. Turn off the Midland Highway onto Lima East Road at Swanpool. Follow Lima East Road for approximately 19km until you reach Goodes Track located on the right. Turn right at Goodes Track and follow for 2km until you reach the intersection of Goodes and Rocky Ned Track, veer right and follow Rocky Ned Track for 1km until you reach your destination Rocky Ned 2 camp site. Please note from Goodes Track it is 4WD access only.

g: Walk · 0.8 km return · under 1 hr · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occassional steps · Limited signage
properties.d: A rocky outcrop east of Buchan with views across the valley.
properties.a: Follow the Basin Rd east from Buchan, turn onto the Old Basin Rd. The access track is approx. 2km from this intersection and it can be rough and potholed. The outcrop is a 400m walk from the informal car park.

g: Walk · 1.4 km return · 45 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Gentle hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Located in the heart of the Big River State Forest, this gentle walk follows the banks of Big River through forests of Peppermint and opens to a picturesque cascading waterfall.
properties.a: From Melbourne take the Maroondah Hwy, turn right to Thornton and turn onto the Goulburn Valley Highway, then right onto Eildon-Jamieson road. Big River road is 30 kilometres from the Highway. Turn right into Big River Road and follow the gravel road for 11.7 km veering right to Enochs Point. Access from the south via Marysville and Woods Point road requires 4 Wheel Drive from 25 Mile Creek.

g: Walk · 0.5 km return · 10 min · Grade 2.2
properties.t: Well formed track · Flat · No steps · Limited signage
properties.d: Take a slow walk along the meandering Goulburn river, peer into the shallow water and you may be able to spot a fish swimming past. Walk past the mini golf and try your luck at a hole in one, pass through some historic mining relics of yester year and finish up at the helipad which was once a tennis court.
properties.a: Begin the walk from the Mini golf course in the centre of town.

properties.n: Far East Gippsland Backroad Tour - The Mighty Snowy - Sandy Point Tk
g: 4WD · 14.4 km return · 1–4 hrs · Difficult (Black Diamond)
properties.d: For 4WDs and drivers with reasonable 4WD experience or 4WD training. The Sandy Point side trip provides access to a beautiful section of the Snowy River and to camping on the western banks of the Snowy River. Here you can enjoy your lunch or stay a few days and enjoy a paddle on the Snowy River.
properties.a: Turn off the Buchan-Orbost Road onto Sandy Point Track and travel 7.2km to reach Sandy Point Campground. Sections on the side trip are unsuitable for caravans due to roads being narrow and steep.

g: Walk · 10.4 km one way · 4 hrs · Grade 4
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · Occasional steps · Sign posted
properties.d: This 11km walk is great for the experienced bushwalker, following the Howqua Valley between Running Creek and Howqua Hills Track. Take in the breathtaking scenery of the surrounding hills and the river below you. There are some short steep hills and small obstacles along the path.
properties.a: To Running Creek - from Mansfield follow the Woods Point Road toward Jamieson. At the Howqua Bridge turn left onto the Howqua River Road, follow for approx 6kms. Continue onto Steiners Rd for 2 kms and turn left into Running Creek.

g: Walk · 0.6 km return · 20 min · Grade 1
properties.t: Well formed track · Flat · No steps · Clearly sign posted
properties.d: This short loop, built for all-abilities, follows a formed gravel path with rest stops and interpretive signs along the way. An all-abilities 600m loop through local forest. The track gradient has been designed for wheelchairs on a compacted gravel surface.
properties.a: Access is via the Great Alpine Rd approx 2km from Bruthen township.

g: Walk · 0.35 km one way · 12 min · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track · Flat · No steps · Sign posted
properties.d: Walking track linking the Cassinia and Sec camping areas

g: Walk · 4.5 km one way · 1–4 hrs · Grade 3
properties.t: Formed track some obstacles · Short steep hills · No steps · Sign posted
properties.a: The Donkey Orchid walking track starts with the Elevator walking track at the west end of the Mt Taylor Mountain bike park. It starts on the left hand side of Lookout Road where the clear area meets the forest. The Donkey Orchid walking track is 4.5 km long and is a loop . The end is beside the large pine trees near the entrance at Bullumwaal Rd
